The experimental group received practice-oriented instruction, while the control group studied through conventional teaching methods. Subsequently, the developed lesson plans and didactic materials were incorporated into an approved 80-hour professional development course completed by 25 school and university teachers from different regions, who provided feedback on their applicability in real biology teaching practice. The findings support the effectiveness of adapting practice-oriented pedagogical approaches for strengthening practical competence in biology teacher education in Kazakhstan.

TI A New Scale in Education (Social Science)
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF COGNITIVE RESEARCH IN SCIENCE ENGINEERING AND
   EDUCATION-IJCRSEE
LA English
DT Article
DE binary choice; intervals; measurements; new scale; social science
ID RATING-SCALES; PSYCHOMETRIC PROPERTIES; RESPONSE CATEGORIES; OPTIMAL
   NUMBER; RELIABILITY
AB This paper introduces a new scale in the social sciences that combines two types of measurements: a binary choice and a relative interval measurement consisting of 10+10 intervals. The scale's relative interval nature allows for differentiation between intervals of 10 +/- 10, expressed based on the principle of deciles. This approach provides a more nuanced differentiation between degrees compared to traditional Likert scales. The paper also discusses a coding method and includes graphical representations of the data. An important aspect of the scale is its capacity to categorize responses into positive and negative attitudes (NEGATT and POSATT), enabling separate descriptive and inferential statistical analyses.

This cooperation is particularly evident in corporate cybersecurity and digital forensics. Today, thanks to the inclusion of emotional awareness in artificial intelligence systems, many organizations can more easily monitor the cognitive load of their analysts during critical security situations. Empathic artificial intelligence in corporate cybersecurity is a new force for proactive threat detection, compliance and risk management. It helps analysts to respond to constant cyber threats more effec-tively, and in forensic investigations it offers great support in emotional and behavioral analysis. In this way, in cybercrime inves-tigations, through the observation of anomalies and their patterns, decisions are made with a higher degree of accuracy. How-ever, this technology still faces numerous challenges, such as accurately reading emotional cues, protecting sensitive data, and ensuring ethical management. In any case, well-defined frameworks that promote cooperation between artificial intelligence and humans are the necessity of the present, in order to remove these barriers. It is undeniable that empathic artificial intelligence has the potential to create security ecosystems that are more adequate, reliable and above all focused on human needs. Therefore, in the near future, it will revolutionize the field of corporate cybersecurity operations and digital forensics, but only if it is smartly implemented.

TI Criminal Treatment of The Misuse of Artificial Intelligence in The
   Creation of Pornographic Content and the Psychological Consequences on
   the Victim
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF COGNITIVE RESEARCH IN SCIENCE ENGINEERING AND
   EDUCATION-IJCRSEE
LA English
DT Article
DE artificial inteligence; deepfakes; pornographic content; criminal
   protection; psychological consequences; prevention
AB The abuse of artificial intelligence in the creation of pornographic content represents a modern form of socially dangerous behavior that requires an adequate criminal law response and an interdisciplinary approach. The development of generative technologies has enabled the creation of highly realistically manipulated or completely synthetic content, which opens up new types of violation of the right to privacy, dignity and personal safety. These forms of abuse include the use of "deepfake" technology, the digital manipulation of existing visual materials, as well as the generation of content that imitates real people without their knowledge or consent, thereby further complicating the determination of responsibility and the protection of victims. The current criminal legal framework is based on the protection of sexual freedom, honor and reputation, as well as the protection of minors, whereby the question of its normative completeness and effectiveness in the context of accelerated technological development and new forms of digital violence is raised. In addition to the legal aspect, this phenomenon is also characterized by pronounced psychological and victimological effects, which are reflected in the impairment of mental health, the feeling of stigmatization, the loss of a sense of security and the long-term consequences for the social functioning of the victims. The work is methodologically based on a theoretical analysis of relevant positions in domestic and foreign literature, a normative analysis of valid legal regulations, as well as on empirical research conducted among students using the survey method. Descriptive analysis was used in the processing and interpretation of collected data, with the application of inductive and deductive methods in order to draw conclusions. Special attention was paid to examining respondents' views on the social danger of this phenomenon, their level of information, as well as the perception of the need to improve criminal law regulations. The aim of the work is to point out the shortcomings of the existing criminal legal framework, as well as the need for its normative improvement and the development of more effective preventive and protective mechanisms.

TI Managerial Information Use and Innovation in Service Microenterprises:
   Implications for Learning, Competence Development, and Quality
   Improvement
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF COGNITIVE RESEARCH IN SCIENCE ENGINEERING AND
   EDUCATION-IJCRSEE
LA English
DT Article
DE managerial learning; managerial competencies; business information use;
   innovation management; quality improvement; service microenterprises
AB Managerial learning and competence development are important for service microenterprises seeking to use business infor-mation effectively, adopt innovations, and improve their operations. This study examines managerial perceptions of information use, innovation, institutional support, and professional development needs in service microenterprises in Serbia, with particular attention to their implications for learning, competence development, and quality improvement. A descriptive survey was conducted from June to December 2024 using a convenience sample of 224 owners, directors, managers, and other representatives of microenterprises located in three municipalities of Belgrade. Data were collected through a structured closed-ended questionnaire and analysed using descriptive statistics. Results show that innovation management was highly valued as a contributor to competitiveness, while technological processes and customer-oriented changes received particularly favourable as-sessments. Respondents associated innovation with market expansion, service quality, operational flexibility, and efficiency, but also identified financial, technological, and knowledge-related constraints. Institutional support was considered particularly important through financial incentives, assistance with technology acquisition, and access to financing. Training preferences focused on export activities, public procurement, marketing and sales, quality standards, and financial management, indicating demand for practically applicable managerial competencies. Business information was also recognized as relevant to successful operations. Overall, the findings indicate that quality improvement in service microenterprises can be supported by strengthening managerial competencies, information use, innovation capacity, and continuing professional learning.

TI Career Perspectives of Teacher Education Students: Choice, Satisfaction
   and Expectations
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF COGNITIVE RESEARCH IN SCIENCE ENGINEERING AND
   EDUCATION-IJCRSEE
LA English
DT Article
DE intention of performing work; perceptions of the teaching profession;
   the importance of work; satisfaction with the choice of a study
   programme and studies
ID PRESERVICE TEACHERS; MOTIVATION; SCALE; PROFESSION; COMMITMENT; OUTCOMES
AB The aim of this study was to examine the perceptions of the teaching profession, satisfaction with the choice of a study programme, and desirable work values in students in their final years of various areas of teacher education studies. The study participants were 443 students in their final year of teacher education studies in the Republic of Croatia. The participants filled out the questionnaires designed to examine their intentions of finding a job in their professional field, their satisfaction with the chosen study programme, the perception of the support received from their surroundings, their satisfaction with a study programme, and the perception of the teaching profession and desirable work values. The findings have shown that students tend to rank highly expert career and high demand of the teaching profession, while they give the lowest ranking to the social status of teachers and their salary. Statistically significant differences were found in almost all of the examined variables with regard to the area of study (interdisciplinary, humanistic, STEM, social). The perceptions of students who intend to find employment in schools are statistically different in comparison with those of students who do not intend to or who are not sure whether they would work in schools, with regard to their satisfaction with the chosen study programme and studies, and their perceptions of the important work values. The logistic regression analysis results indicate that satisfaction with the chosen study programme is the most important factor contributing to students' intentions to find employment in school. The findings highlight the importance of strengthening professional orientation and providing support to students during their studies, while future research should further examine the factors underlying satisfaction with the choice of a study programme.

TI The Betelgeuse Enigma: The Betelbuddy Hypothesis
SO RESONANCE-JOURNAL OF SCIENCE EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE <italic>alpha</italic> Orionis; Betelgeuse; Milky Way; supernova;
   betelbuddy; companion star; <italic>beta</italic> Orionis
AB In the past six years, Betelgeuse has been in the news and drawn significant public interest. Starting in October 2019, Betelgeuse underwent a striking dimming event, fading from magnitude 0.5 to 1.7 by mid-February 2020-a threefold decrease in brightness! This gave rise to a number of speculative debates that the star was on the verge of a supernova, a moment of eerie quiet before the cosmic outburst. In a previous article, the author discussed the most accepted explanation for the dimming caused by episodic mass loss that released large dust grains, which obscured Betelgeuse's light and made it appear fainter. This interpretation suggested that the dimming was not a precursor to a supernova, as Betelgeuse is likely still far from reaching that stageSurprisingly, after that, Betelgeuse gradually brightened up in April 2023 with a peak of 0.1 V band magnitude and later dimmed to about 0.7 V band magnitude in 2024.Betelgeuse has two periods of variability: A short one of about 400 days and a longer one lasting around 6 years. Based on archival data, two independent studies proposed that the longer period, probably the long secondary period (LSP), is due to an undetected low-mass binary companion. Also, radial velocity and astrometric data of Betelgeuse also point to a companion. Recent observations of Betelgeuse made with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) showed that Betelgeuse is rotating at about 5 km s-1. It was proposed that Betelgeuse's high rotation rate is caused by a merger with a lower mass companion or gravitational interactions with a companion which could 'spin up' the larger star.HST and Chandra observations were made to find the companion, which were unsuccessful. On 21 July 2025, the existence of the companion star was confirmed with direct imaging, for the first time, by the Alopeke instrument on the 8.1 m Gemini North telescope. The companion is 6 magnitudes fainter than Betelgeuse and orbits close to Betelgeuse itself, within the supergiant star's extended outer atmosphere. The stellar companion was detected at an angular separation of 52 mas and a position angle of 115 degrees east of north. These measurements, along with its brightness, being roughly 6 magnitudes fainter than Betelgeuse at 466 nm, are in excellent agreement with dynamical predictions. Although this was only a 1.5 sigma detection, the agreement in the companion's appearance, separation, position angle, magnitude difference, and estimated mass is reasonable, making the result tentatively acceptable. The next optimum period for observations is November 2027, when we hope to get better observations. The companion star is of the same age as Betelgeuse, 10 million years, but on a totally different stage of evolution, as it differs in mass. While Betelgeuse is in the later stage of evolution as a red supergiant, this is a star not yet born-a premain-sequence star. However, its fate is sealed: Betelgeuse will cannibalise it in 10,000 years. This article describes the interesting twists and turns of this study and what lies ahead for Betelgeuse and its companion, Betelbuddy, or Siwarha!

TI Unlocking Biodiversity Through Environmental DNA Metabarcoding
SO RESONANCE-JOURNAL OF SCIENCE EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Biodiversity loss; species diversity; DNA barcodes; environmental DNA;
   metabarcoding; application
AB This article introduces the exciting world of environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding, a cutting-edge tool for studying biodiversity without even seeing the organisms. It explains how tiny traces of DNA left behind by animals, plants, or microbes in water, soil, or air can be collected and used to identify what species are or were present in that environment. The process is broken down step-by-step: from collecting and properly preserving the samples to amplifying the DNA and sequencing it. The article highlights why sample quality is crucial and explains how common mistakes, such as missing PCR controls or failing to account for inhibitors, can compromise results. It also discusses how long eDNA persists in the environment and the factors that cause it to break down. Despite some challenges, such as incomplete reference databases, eDNA is already being used to estimate which species are present, how abundant they are, and even to reconstruct past ecosystems. By combining eDNA methods with high-tech sequencing and powerful computer tools, scientists are now able to monitor biodiversity more effectively and often more easily than with traditional methods. It is a fast-growing field that is opening up new possibilities in ecology, conservation, and even in archaeology.

TI Linear Programming Through the Lens of Theoretical Computer Science

LA English

   optimization; graphical method
AB Pre-university-level (grade 11 or 12) students are introduced to linear programming (LP) as a tool for formulating simple combinatorial optimization problems and solving them using the graphical method. TI Evolution of Chemical Thought
SO RESONANCE-JOURNAL OF SCIENCE EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE History of chemistry; chemical thought; chemical sciences; metallurgy;
   materials science; history of medicine; ancient civilizations; alchemy
AB Chemistry, as we know it today, has evolved over several millennia. Its beginnings can be traced to practices in metallurgy and materials, and to the exploration of natural sources in the context of medicines for various diseases by ancient civilizations such as the Mesopotamian, Egyptian, Indian, and Chinese. In this article, the attempt is primarily to outline these practices across the four civilizations. Due to extensive cross-country communication, modern science is advancing in parallel across the world. However, in ancient times (prior to 1000 BCE), it most likely developed in isolation in various regions of the world. In section 2.1, the discussion centers around the practices of the Mesopotamian and Egyptian civilizations during the fourth and third millennia BCE. In Section 2.2, the discussion focuses on the Indus Valley civilization, and in Section 2.3, a brief discussion of the achievements of the Yellow River (Chinese) civilization follows. All four civilizations excelled in exploring nature and identifying useful metals, materials, and medicines. Available information about each civilization is summarized according to achievements in 'metals and materials' and 'medicinal' sub-sections.The Mesopotamians and Egyptians have left behind an enormous wealth of information in cuneiform tablets and papyri, respectively. However, a lack of similar documentary evidence on the Indus Valley has made it harder for historians to develop a more comprehensive picture. Section 3 primarily discusses the Indian and Chinese civilizations from similar to 1200 BCE to similar to 1700 CE. During this period, textual and other archaeological evidence make it easier to reconstruct the chemical practices of both civilizations. Details of chemical practices, the use of instruments, and explorations of the inanimate and animate worlds are very rich. Although only a small part of this evidence has been examined, metallurgical practices, pottery, perfume-making, fermentation, and medicinal practices reached new heights in both civilizations. The discovery of new metals like mercury, zinc, etc., contributed to the development of new materials and medicines. Ras & amacr;yana (in Indian tradition) and neidan and waidan (Chinese tradition) provided a framework for both (al)chemical and iatrochemical practices. There is also the likelihood of exchange of ideas among India, China, and the Arab empire during the 500 CE-1200 CE period. This article focuses mainly on the discoveries/observations. We will take up the discussion of the theoretical frameworks for the above-mentioned practices in some detail in a later article and consider especially the rich discussion of atomism in the Indian tradition.

TI Quantum Computing for Molecular Systems
SO RESONANCE-JOURNAL OF SCIENCE EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Quantum computing; quantum algorithm; variational quantum eigensolver;
   hardware-specific ansatz; coupled-cluster ansatz
AB This third part of the review article series 'Quantum Computing for Molecular Systems', discusses quantum algorithms. In particular, it focuses on the variational quantum algorithms (VQAs), which represent the most widely used class of quantum algorithms for near-term quantum devices. Building upon the mapping of fermionic Hamiltonians to qubit Hamiltonians (in Part II), here we explore how to employ VQAs to approximate the ground-state energy of molecular systems. We discuss the design of chemically motivated ansatzes, such as the unitary coupled-cluster approach, alongside hardware-efficient alternatives, highlighting trade-offs among expressibility, circuit depth, and resource requirements. We also elucidate the current hardware limitations, available quantum platforms, and hybrid quantum-classical approaches that are facilitating the early realization of quantum computing applications in molecular sciences.

   Taksims
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF MUSIC EDUCATION

DT Article
DE Formative assessment; improvisation; interview; music education; taksim;
   video recordings
AB In this research, I aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of using video recordings in the process of formative assessment of taksims performed within the maqams covered in a Turkish music theory course. Taksim entails a performance aligned with the melodic movement features of a given maqam, adhering to its rules, yet allowing for improvised expression without a rhythmic structure. Maqam can be defined as the creation of musical phrases with a number of special rules by using certain sounds. Taksim studies are carried out in Turkish Music Conservatories, generally in the third and fourth grades, for the practice of the maqams taught in Turkish music theory courses. In my study, I employed observation, retrospective verbal protocol analysis, and interviews. I analyzed data using the content analysis approach on ATLAS.ti software. From my investigation, I deduced that analyzing videos during the formative assessment stage proved beneficial in identifying errors and enhancing skills such as error recognition, intonation, musicality, melody creation, motivation, and confidence.

TI Kayanapussana Satipatthana and the Buddhist practices of Samadhi
   and Sati as foundational practices in the development of Thai musical
   skills
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF MUSIC EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Buddhism; meditation; music; pedagogy; Samadhi; Sati; Thai music
AB The Buddhist Vipassana technique of Kayanupassana Satipatthana is used to develop samadhi (concentration) and sati (awareness) in the practices of Thai classical music (dontri Thai) teachers working in a Thai primary school and the specialist music school in a Thai university. While previous studies have explored the use of mediation as a means of alleviating stress or spiritual progress, the techniques described here are adapted in this dontri Thai pedagogy to help musicians optimize learning and performing through the cultivation of concentration, awareness, and bodily control. Within this pedagogy, sharpened concentration leads to heightened awareness which allows greater insight into the students' state of mind, musical sounds, and sensory feelings in their bodies. This enable performers to reproduce what is conceptualized as the "ideal" sound. Students commence musical training by practicing meditation while producing a single note, a short melody, or a technical skill. The task is repeated until the tripartite goal of mental and physical immersion and the production of the ideal sound is achieved. The four key components of the method are integrated within a holistic and iterative learning process in which the student progressively develops the ability to focus on all relevant elements in a single moment.

TI The Role of Negative Automatic Thoughts and Metacognitions in Explaining
   Social Anxiety
SO CUKUROVA UNIVERSITY FACULTY OF EDUCATION JOURNAL
LA English
DT Article
DE Social anxiety; Metacognitive Model; Cognitive Behavioral Model;
   Metacognitive beliefs; Automatic thoughts
ID SELF-FOCUSED ATTENTION; COGNITIVE THERAPY; DISORDER; QUESTIONNAIRE;
   RELIABILITY; ADOLESCENTS; LONELINESS; DEPRESSION; VALIDITY; BELIEFS
AB This study examines the unique and combined predictive levels of negative automatic thoughts and metacognitive beliefs regarding social anxiety symptoms. The research included 424 participants (255 females, 169 males). Findings from regression models revealed that metacognitive beliefs accounted for 23% of the variance in social anxiety, while automatic thoughts accounted for 22%. When both automatic thoughts and metacognitions were included in the model simultaneously, they jointly explained 29% of the variance in social anxiety. Among the automatic thoughts, Self-Oriented Automatic Thoughts (beta= .29, p< .001) and Loneliness (beta= .34, p< .001) were significant predictors. In terms of metacognitive variables, the Need for Thought Control (beta= .48, p< .001) and Cognitive Awareness (beta= -.11, p < .001) significantly predicted social anxiety symptoms. When both automatic thoughts and metacognitive beliefs were included in the model together, only the Need for Thought Control (beta= .35, p< .001) remained a significant predictor of social anxiety symptoms. The results indicate that negative automatic thoughts and metacognitive beliefs explain social anxiety at similar levels, with the Need for Thought Control showing the strongest statistical impact. This finding is significant for future research and intervention strategies.

TI Ethical Blind Spots of Canadian School Principals
SO CUKUROVA UNIVERSITY FACULTY OF EDUCATION JOURNAL
LA English
DT Article
DE Canadian Schools; School Principals; Ethical Dilemmas; Ethical Blind
   Spots
ID DECISION-MAKING; ORGANIZATIONS
AB The aim of this research is to examine the ethical blind spots of school principals in Canada. To achieve this aim, the study was designed using a phenomenological design which is a qualitative research method. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with seven school principals working in schools with diverse characteristics in the city of Toronto, located in the Ontario province of Canada. TI The Use of Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge in Turkish
   Language Courses: Teachers' Perspectives
SO CUKUROVA UNIVERSITY FACULTY OF EDUCATION JOURNAL
LA English
DT Article
DE Content knowledge; Pedagogical knowledge; Technological knowledge;
   Technological Pedagogical Content; Knowledge; Turkish language teacher
AB The current educational paradigm requires teachers to go beyond being mere transmitters of knowledge and instead become educational leaders who structure learning processes, uncover students' individual competencies, and support their holistic development. In this context, teachers are expected not only to possess content knowledge, pedagogical knowledge, and technological knowledge, but also to integrate and harmonize these three domains within teaching and learning processes. This study aims to determine Turkish language teachers' views regarding their technological pedagogical content knowledge (TPACK). The study was designed in the phenomenological design of qualitative research. The participants consisted of 27 Turkish language teachers working in the province of Duzce. Data were collected using a semi-structured interview form developed based on the TPACK model. The analysis revealed that, despite the influence of traditional educational perspectives, Turkish language teachers strive to implement student-centered approaches; they believe they possess strong content knowledge; and, in terms of technopedagogical competence, they reported using technology more frequently for lesson planning, applying student-centered methods, and selecting instructional strategies. However, it was observed that the technological tools employed were mostly geared toward passive consumption, while tools that promote active participation and creativity were used only to a limited extent. Additionally, although technology integration in Turkish language lessons was found to enhance comprehension skills, it remained inadequate for fostering production-and interaction-based skills. Overall, the findings suggest that Turkish language teachers' TPACK competencies are limited.

TI Examining the Mediating Role of Hope in the Relationship Between
   Cognitive Flexibility and Life Satisfaction
SO CUKUROVA UNIVERSITY FACULTY OF EDUCATION JOURNAL
LA English
DT Article
DE Cognitive Flexibility; Hope; Life Satisfaction; Young Adults
ID MENTAL-HEALTH; HOPELESSNESS; PERSONALITY; HAPPINESS; STRESS; WORK
AB With the emergence of positive psychology, there has been a growing emphasis on understanding not only the problems individuals face but also the positive aspects of their lives. In this context, one of the notable concepts is life satisfaction. The present study sought to understand the psychological mechanisms explaining life satisfaction among young adults in the Turkish context. The research examined the role of hope in the relationship between cognitive flexibility, a key psychological resource, and life satisfaction. The study, designed with a correlational model, included 311 volunteer young adults. Data were collected using the Personal Information Form, the Satisfaction with Life Scale, the Dispositional Hope Scale, and the Cognitive Control and Flexibility Questionnaire. The data were analyzed through descriptive statistics, correlation analyses, and mediation effects tested using Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression-based approach and the Bootstrap Method to determine statistical significance. The findings indicated significant positive relations among cognitive flexibility, hope, and life satisfaction. Mediation analyses demonstrated that hope played a mediating role in the relationship between cognitive flexibility and life satisfaction, and that cognitive flexibility and hope together explained 12% of life satisfaction. The study enriches the existing body of knowledge by underlining the importance of cognitive flexibility and hope as psychological resources in explaining life satisfaction.

TI An Investigation on the Indicators of Reading Comprehension in Turkish
   Monolingual and Turkish-Arabic Bilingual Children
SO CUKUROVA UNIVERSITY FACULTY OF EDUCATION JOURNAL
LA English
DT Article
DE Simultaneous Bilingualism; Reading Development; Reading Comprehension;
   Vocabulary Knowledge; Morphosyntactic Awareness; Phonological Memory
ID AUTOMATIZED NAMING RAN; PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS; MORPHOLOGICAL AWARENESS;
   VOCABULARY INSTRUCTION; SIMPLE VIEW; SKILLS; LITERACY; ABILITY; FLUENCY;
   MEMORY
AB The present study investigated the role of phonological awareness, phonological memory, rapid automatized naming, morphosyntactic awareness, processing speed, vocabulary knowledge and word reading fluency in Turkish reading comprehension. Cross-sectional data were collected from 8-9-year-old, second-grade Turkish-Arabic simultaneous bilingual children and Turkish monolingual children. This variation may have implications for reading assessment and instruction.

AB Understanding the internal processes of learning is a fundamental aspect of explaining individual development and evaluating learning activities. TI The Effects of Sports Participation on High School Entrance Examination
   Candidates' Attention Levels and Test Anxietye
SO CUKUROVA UNIVERSITY FACULTY OF EDUCATION JOURNAL
LA English
DT Article
DE Exam Anxiety; Student; Attention; Sports Participation
ID PERFORMANCE; EXERCISE; BRAIN
AB The High School Entrance Exam (LGS), which is used for the transition to secondary education in T & uuml;rkiye, plays a decisive role in students' academic placement processes. It is frequently emphasized in the literature that such high-stakes, centralized examinations may increase students' test anxiety. Therefore, students' test anxiety are expected to be relatively higher. The demonstration of the positive effects of sports on attention and anxiety in many studies has led to an expectation that students who engage in sports will have lower levels of anxiety and higher levels of attention. This study was designed to examine the test anxiety and attention levels of students preparing for the LGS. This study, conducted using a quantitative research method, included a total of 320 students (140 female and 180 male) selected from private tutoring centers in Mu & scedil; province who will take the LGS in 2025. The d2 Attention Test and the Test Anxiety Scale were used as data collection tools. The obtained data were analyzed using the SPSS 26, and parametric tests were applied in accordance with the results. According to the results of the study, it was determined that participation in sports had a positive effect on attention, while it increased test anxiety. It was found that male students were more successful in terms of sustaining attention and efficiency, whereas female students had higher levels of test anxiety and a greater tendency to make errors. In addition, it was observed that academically successful students also had higher levels of test anxiety. Overall, it was concluded that students who participated in sports had higher attention scores, lower error rates, and that there was a weak correlation between attention and anxiety.

TI Early Childhood Education Pre-Service Teachers' Epistemological Beliefs
   and Attitudes Toward Science Teaching: An Explanatory Sequential
   Mixed-Methods Study
SO CUKUROVA UNIVERSITY FACULTY OF EDUCATION JOURNAL
LA English
DT Article
DE Epistemological Beliefs; Attitudes Toward Science Teaching; Pre-Service
   Teachers Education; Mixed-Methods Research
AB The aim of this study is to examine how Early Childhood Education Pre-Service Teachers' (ECEPSTs) epistemological beliefs are related to their attitudes toward science teaching in the context of specific demographic variables. A mixed-methods research design was adopted, integrating both quantitative and qualitative data. Data were collected through the Attitude Scale Toward Science Teaching, the Epistemological Beliefs Scale, and a semi-structured interview form. Quantitative findings indicated a significant difference in ECEPSTs' epistemological beliefs only in relation to their engagement with scientific content via social media and internet platforms. Regarding attitudes toward science teaching, significant differences were identified based on grade level, engaging in scientific discussions with peers, following scientific content outside of class, and watching science-related content on social media. Moreover, a moderate, positive, and significant correlation was found between epistemological beliefs and attitudes toward science teaching. Qualitative findings revealed that ECEPSTs held well-developed epistemological views and demonstrated positive attitudes toward science teaching. Participants emphasized that technological advancements have facilitated access to information, thereby enhancing their engagement with scientific content and positively shaping their epistemological beliefs. They also reported that acquiring knowledge from various digital sources prior to science instruction supported their attitudes toward science teaching. Overall, the findings indicate a strong alignment between the quantitative and qualitative data.

TI Depressive Symptoms in 5-6-Year-Old Children: The Role of Family
   Resilience and Family Functioning
SO CUKUROVA UNIVERSITY FACULTY OF EDUCATION JOURNAL
LA English
DT Article
DE Early Childhood; Depressive Symptoms; Family Resilience; Family
   Functioning; Hierarchical Regression Model
ID SELF-REGULATION; MENTAL-HEALTH; CHILDHOOD; MODEL; ANXIETY; STRESS;
   ASSOCIATION; ADOLESCENTS; COMPETENCE; VALIDATION
AB This study examined the relationships between depressive symptoms observed in children aged 5-6 and two family-related variables: family resilience and perceived family functioning. Using a quantitative correlational survey design, the study was conducted with 255 parents selected through criterion sampling and voluntary participation. Data were collected through the Childhood Depressive Symptom Assessment Scale, the Family Resilience Scale, and the Perceived Family Functioning Scale. Following assumption testing, Pearson correlation, multiple linear regression, and a three-step hierarchical multiple regression analysis controlling for demographic variables were performed. The findings indicated that several subdimensions of family resilience and family functioning were significantly associated with distinct patterns of depressive symptoms in children. In particular, self-efficacy and commitment to life emerged as more salient components of family resilience, whereas intra-familial communication and positive affect, together with boundaries, stood out as stronger predictors within family functioning. Overall, the results suggest that family processes in early childhood are meaningfully related to children's depressive symptoms and underscore the importance of family-focused preventive and supportive interventions.

TI Protective Factors Against Learned Helplessness in Emerging Adulthood:
   Grit, Self-Compassion and Gratitude
SO CUKUROVA UNIVERSITY FACULTY OF EDUCATION JOURNAL
LA English
DT Article
DE Learned Helplessness; Self-Compassion; Gratitude; Grit; Gradual
   Regression
ID PERFECTIONISM; ASSOCIATION; OPTIMISM; ESCAPE; SCALE
AB The aim of this research is to examine whether the variables of self-compassion, gratitude, and grit have a protective effect against learned helplessness among individuals in emerging adulthood. The study employed a quantitative method with a descriptive research design. The study group consists of 356 individuals in the emerging adulthood period. Of the participants, 254 are female (71.3%) and 102 are male (28.7%). We found that the learned helplessness variable had significant negative correlations with all other variables. According to the results of the stepwise multiple regression analysis, we found grit, self-compassion, and gratitude as the predictors of learned helplessness. Accordingly, in the first model, grit alone predicts 42.2% of the variance in learned helplessness; grit and self-compassion together predict 47.7%; and grit, selfcompassion, and gratitude together predict 48.3% of the variance. All models were found to be statistically significant (p <.001). Addressing factors that protect individuals from learned helplessness may be helpful in preventive work, especially for those working in the field of mental health. We believe that intervention studies that consider these factors will make meaningful contributions to well-being research at the individual and societal levels.

TI Qualitative Study on the Professional Ethics Awareness of Graphic Design
   Students
SO CUKUROVA UNIVERSITY FACULTY OF EDUCATION JOURNAL
LA English
DT Article
DE Graphic Design; Ethical Principles; Ethical Awareness; Ethics Education
AB The aim of this study is to investigate the level and characteristics of the professional ethics awareness of students enrolled in graphic design departments, in which professional ethics courses have been found to occupy a limited place in the curriculum. Designed as a phenomenological study, one of the qualitative research designs, the research was conducted with a total of 25 fourth-year graphic design students selected through purposive sampling from state universities located in five different geographical regions of T & uuml;rkiye. The data were collected through face-to-face semi-structured interviews and analysed by means of content analysis. The findings revealed that, although prospective graphic designers possess a general awareness of the concept of ethics, they are unable to transfer this awareness to professional practice. In particular, it was determined that the students have marked deficiencies in knowledge concerning such matters as copyright, font licensing, original design and legal responsibilities, and that their awareness of the Law on Intellectual and Artistic Works (FSEK) and of the concept of plagiarism remains extremely limited. By contrast, the great majority of the participants stated that an ethics course should be incorporated into graphic design programmes. Considered as a whole, these findings lead to the conclusion that systematically strengthening the teaching of ethics in graphic design education constitutes an important necessity.

TI The Role of Mindfulness and Contrast Avoidance in Individuals' Attitudes
   Toward Psychotherapy
SO CUKUROVA UNIVERSITY FACULTY OF EDUCATION JOURNAL
LA English
DT Article
DE Mindfulness; Contrast avoidance; Thoughts on psychotherapy
ID EXPERIENTIAL AVOIDANCE; COMMITMENT THERAPY; SELF-REPORT; ACCEPTANCE;
   METAANALYSIS; DROPOUT; MODEL; WILLINGNESS; PREDICTORS; AWARENESS
AB The Contrast Avoidance Model is a contemporary model proposing that individuals maintain a negative affective state because they perceive emotional fluctuations as threatening and consider remaining in this state potentially beneficial. Maintaining a chronic negative mood can prevent diverse emotional experiences during the psychotherapy process or lead to the avoidance of positive emotions that could potentially emerge with recovery. This can lead to the emergence of negative beliefs and attitudes about the therapy process and, indirectly, lead to the termination of the therapy process. In this context, mindfulness is thought to be a significant determinant of individuals' thoughts about psychotherapy, but this relationship may be shaped by the tendencies toward contrast avoidance. Therefore, this study aimed to examine the mediating role of contrast avoidance in the effect of mindfulness on thoughts about psychotherapy. The study sample consisted of 281 female and 124 male participants aged 18-60 years, with a mean age of 29.39 years (SD = 8.26). The study utilized the Thoughts About Psychotherapy Scale, the Contrast Avoidance Scale, and the Mindful Attention Awareness Scale. Structural equation modeling was used to analyze the data. Data were analyzed using SPSS and AMOS. The study found a significant relationship between mindful awareness, contrast avoidance, and thoughts about psychotherapy. The study revealed that contrast avoidance mediated the effect of mindfulness on attitudes toward psychotherapy. These results suggest that mindfulness practices can contribute to the therapy process by reducing individuals' tendencies toward contrast avoidance behaviors.

TI Intrinsic kinematics: coordinate-free acceleration direction in two and
   three dimensions
SO EUROPEAN JOURNAL OF PHYSICS
LA English
DT Article
DE intrinsic kinematics; Frenet-Serret frame; acceleration decomposition;
   coordinate-free mechanics; curvature and torsion; curvilinear motion;
   classical mechanics pedagogy
AB Standard treatments of curvilinear motion decompose acceleration into tangential and normal components, but the resulting components are seldom assembled into an explicit expression for the global direction of the acceleration vector in coordinate-free terms. This tutorial collects, organizes, and works through such an expression for both planar curves and space curves in R-3, with worked exercises intended for classroom use. Using the Frenet-Serret frame, curvature kappa, and torsion tau (Frenet 1852 J. Math. Pures Appl. 17 437-47), (Serret 1851 J. Math. Pures Appl. 16 193-207), (Struik 1988 Lectures on Classical Differential Geometry), (Kreyszig 1991 Differential Geometry), (do Carmo 1976 Differential Geometry of Curves and Surfaces) we present four results. First, for a smooth planar curve, the absolute direction of acceleration is assembled into the exact, coordinate-free formula theta a(s)=Theta 0+integral s0s kappa d sigma+atan2(kappa s(center dot)2,s & uml;), separating an intrinsic tilt phi=atan2(kappa s(center dot)2,s & uml;) from an extrinsic path orientation Theta(s). Second, for any C2 space curve, the acceleration vector is confined to the osculating plane: the binormal component aB=a & sdot;B vanishes identically. Third, the acceleration tilt phi is tau-independent and remains fully intrinsic in three dimensions; the absolute spatial direction of acceleration is a =cos phi T(s)+sin phi phi N(s), where T,N are determined by integrating both kappa and tau. Fourth, setting tau equivalent to 0 reduces the three-dimensional formula to the planar formula exactly-the planar result is a strict special case, not an independent result. Worked examples on a circular path and a circular helix confirm consistency with direct Cartesian computation.

TI Seeing through the light cone: visualizing electromagnetic fields in
   special relativity
SO EUROPEAN JOURNAL OF PHYSICS
LA English
DT Article
DE special relativity; electromagnetism; Lorentz transformation;
   relativistic dynamics; computer simulation; light cone visualization;
   educational physics tools
ID TIME
AB The theoretical framework of electromagnetism played a foundational role in Einstein's development of special relativity. To support conceptual understanding, we present a fully special relativistic computer simulation that visualizes electromagnetic fields from the perspective of a moving observer. In this simulation, the observer perceives the world through their past light cone (PLC). The electromagnetic field at each point of this PLC is computed from the subluminal motion of point charges at the intersection of their worldlines with the PLC of that point, ensuring causal consistency and Lorentz covariance. Each charged particle-possibly including the observer-then experiences the Lorentz force from the field at its own spacetime location. This approach offers an interactive and intuitive representation of relativistic electromagnetism: it provides insight into how electric and magnetic fields transform across inertial frames, serves as a bridge between abstract formalism and physical intuition, and lends itself to pedagogical use in courses on special relativity or electrodynamics.

AB BACKGROUND:To assess patient safety culture using the Hospital Survey on Patient Safety Culture (HSOPSC) and to examine associations between occupational characteristics, perceived incident-reporting barriers, and overall safety culture scores among healthcare professionals in the United Arab Emirates. MATERIALS AND METHODS:A cross-sectional survey was conducted between January and March 2023 among 629 healthcare professionals in the United Arab Emirates, including physicians, nurses, and allied health professionals, using convenience sampling. Participants completed a sociodemographic and work characteristics questionnaire alongside the HSOPSC. Item-level positive response rates were calculated, and overall HSOPSC mean scores were compared across occupational characteristics and reporting-barrier frequency categories using t-tests and analysis of variance (two-sided; P < 0.05). RESULTS:Reporting of near-miss events was limited (40.1%), despite high levels of perceived interpersonal respect (84.2%). Respondents reporting barriers seldom demonstrated significantly higher patient safety culture scores across the majority of barrier domains (P < 0.05). CONCLUSION:Targeted system-level interventions, including simplification of reporting processes, strengthening nonpunitive culture, and improving feedback mechanisms, are recommended to enhance reporting and patient safety outcomes.

TI Enhancing first-aid self-efficacy: A randomized trial comparing three
   interactive educational ınterventions
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Accidents; emergency medical services; first aid; home; nursing
   education; self-efficacy; students
ID BASIC LIFE-SUPPORT; STUDENTS; SKILLS
AB BACKGROUND: Effective first-aid education is a critical public health strategy to reduce the burden on emergency services. This study aimed to evaluate and compare the effectiveness of three interactive first-aid training modalities (case-, video-, and drama-based) on university students' first-aid self-efficacy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A three-arm randomized controlled trial with a pretest-post-test design was conducted. The study included 93 university students, randomly assigned to three intervention groups (n = 31 each). The intervention groups received six core first-aid topics delivered through case-, video-, or drama-based methods, while the control group received unstructured education. Data were collected using the "First Aid Self-Efficacy Scale." Statistical analysis was performed using analysis of covariance to compare post-test scores while controlling for baseline differences. RESULTS: More than 95% of the participants were unmarried, and more than 50% in each study group were female. Post-test mean scale scores were highest in the case-based group (194.16 +/- 25.17), followed by the video-based (190.61 +/- 24.08), drama-based (168.22 +/- 54.37), and unstructured groups (162.29 +/- 45.19). Baseline sociodemographic assessments revealed a statistically significant difference in gender distribution across groups (p = 0.008). However, after adjusting for these baseline scores, the study results showed no statistically significant differences between the three interactive training groups in total first-aid self-efficacy or its subdimensions at post-test (p > 0.050). While all groups demonstrated a longitudinal improvement in self-efficacy scores from preintervention to postintervention, no single interactive method demonstrated statistical superiority over the others. CONCLUS & imath;ON: Interactive first-aid training, regardless of the specific modality, is effective in enhancing students' self-efficacy. These findings suggest that educators can flexibly employ a range of interactive strategies to achieve comparable outcomes in prehospital emergency care training. Interactive first-aid training meets essential health policy benchmarks for emergency preparedness, offering educators flexible, effective, and interchangeable modalities to enhance public self-efficacy.

TI Differential effects of unilateral forced nostril breathing on
   baroreflex sensitivity and cardiovascular parameters in healthy young
   men: A cross-sectional study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Baroreflex sensitivity; complementary therapies; forced nostril
   breathing
ID HEART-RATE; OBESITY
AB BACKGROUND:Baroreflex sensitivity (BRS) is a crucial marker of autonomic cardiovascular control, and it is also a predictor of cardiovascular risk. Unilateral forced nostril breathing (UFNB) is one of the many types of pranayama, which are breathing techniques in Yoga. This type of breathing can influence autonomic function through hemispheric activation, yet its direct impact on BRS remains unexplored. To assess the immediate effects of left and right UFNB on BRS and cardiovascular parameters in healthy young adult men. MATERIALS AND METHODS:It is a cross-section study, which included 55 healthy adult men (mean age 25.67 +/- 5.89 years). The participants underwent the standardized protocols for measuring BRS, blood pressure, and heart rate during baseline and the 2-minute interventions of left and right UFNB. BRS was measured using the sequence method with Finapres technology. Paired t-tests were used to compare the baseline and the postintervention values. RESULTS:Performing left UFNB significantly increased BRS by 19.6% (P < 0.001, d = 3.63), whereas the blood pressure and heart rate decreased (all P < 0.001), probably indicating profound activation of parasympathetic system. On the other hand, performing the right UFNB decreased BRS by 5.6% (P = 0.012, d = 0.35) and also increased blood pressure and heart rate (all P < 0.01), probably suggesting a sympathetic activation. Waist circumference correlated negatively with the baseline BRS values (r = -0.513, P < 0.001). CONCLUSION:Left UFNB produces substantial immediate improvements in BRS with parasympathetic enhancement, whereas right UFNB induces sympathetic activation. These findings suggest a potential therapeutic application for the use of UFNB in cardiovascular health management as a nonpharmacological intervention.

TI Prediction of phase angle based on body composition: Insights from a
   large population-based registry
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Adipose tissue; body composition; body water; electric impedance;
   muscles
ID BIOELECTRICAL-IMPEDANCE ANALYSIS; ASSOCIATION; BIA
AB BACKGROUND: Phase angle (PhA) is obtained through bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) and is a potential marker of nutritional health and cellular function. We aimed to develop an equation for estimating PhA using body composition parameters, focusing on skeletal muscle mass, body water, and fat mass. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study enrolled participants from the Iranian National Obesity Registry. Data on age, gender, body composition, and BIA measurements were collected using an InBody 770 device. Exclusion criteria included pregnancy, pacemakers, implants, or edema. The study was approved by the Ethics Committee of Mashhad University of Medical Sciences. RESULTS: A total of 5980 participants (28.7% men, 71.3% women) were included. PhA showed the strongest correlations with extracellular water/total body water (ECW/TBW) (r = -0.84, P < 0.001), followed by intracellular water (ICW) (r = 0.62, P < 0.001) and skeletal muscle mass (SMM) (r = 0.62, P < 0.001). Linear regression models revealed a significant negative association between ECW/TBW and PhA (beta = -82.81, P < 0.001), explaining 71% of variance. Adding age (beta = 0.012, P < 0.001) improved the model (R-2 = 0.75), and SMM (beta = 0.039, P < 0.001) further increased explanatory power (R-2 = 0.85). Including body fat mass (BFM) (beta = 0.005, P < 0.001) and height (beta = -0.031, P < 0.001) led to the highest model fit (R-2 = 0.90). CONCLUSION: ECW/TBW, SMM, BFM, age, and height are significant predictors of PhA, with ECW/TBW showing the strongest negative association.

TI Relationship between hypochondriasis and clinical self-efficacy in
   nursing students: A cross-sectional multi-institutional study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Cross-sectional studies; hypochondriasis; nursing student; self-efficacy
AB BACKGROUND: Psychological factors, such as anxiety, depression, and self-esteem, can significantly impact nursing students' clinical self-efficacy. Hypochondriasis emerges as a critical yet understudied factor in the clinical competence of nursing students, warranting further investigation. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between hypochondriasis and clinical self-efficacy among nursing students. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted in nursing schools of West Mazandaran province in 2024. The sample size was 228 nursing students. Data were collected using a personal information form, the standard clinical self-efficacy questionnaire, and the hypochondriasis questionnaire during 2023-2024. Data were analyzed using univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses performed in (Stata Corp LP, College Station, Texas, USA). Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals were calculated. RESULTS: The mean hypochondriasis score among students was 23.43 +/- 10.81. The prevalence of hypochondriasis among nursing students was 54.3%. Univariable logistic regression analysis revealed a significant negative relationship between hypochondriasis and clinical self-efficacy (OR = 0.92, P < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression analysis highlights a significant association between gender (<0.001), academic year (0.021), lower self-efficacy (<0.001), and increased levels of hypochondriasis. CONCLUSIONS: This study reveals a significant inverse link between hypochondriasis and clinical self-efficacy in nursing students, driven by gender, academic year, and GPA. These findings necessitate integrating mental health support and tailored academic strategies into nursing education to alleviate health-related anxieties, bolster clinical confidence, and ultimately improve patient care outcomes by fostering resilient, competent professionals.

TI Efficacy of ginger and fennel in relieving primary dysmenorrhea: A
   triple-blind crossover controlled trial
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Fennel; ginger; herbal remedies; menstrual pain; primary dysmenorrhea;
   randomized controlled trial
AB BACKGROUND: Primary dysmenorrhea, characterized by painful menstrual cramps without underlying pelvic pathology, is common among young women and affects physical and emotional wellbeing. This study was conducted to evaluate and compare the effectiveness of ginger and fennel in relieving primary dysmenorrhea. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A triple-blind crossover clinical trial was conducted from October 2020 to March 2022 at one medical college and two schools in Dehradun, Uttarakhand, India, among 384 young women aged 18-26 years. Participants received ginger (500 mg), fennel (480 mg) or placebo capsules every 8 h during the first three days of menstruation for three cycles, with washout periods between interventions. Pain severity, intensity and duration were assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), Short Form McGill Pain Questionnaire and self-reported pain duration. Data analysis was performed using repeated measures ANOVA and paired t-tests in SPSS version 27, with a significance level set at P < 0.05. RESULTS: A total of 384 participants (mean age: 20.66 +/- 1.66 years) completed the study. Ginger showed the greatest reduction in pain severity, with VAS scores decreasing from 6.14 +/- 1.45 to 3.28 +/- 1.21, followed by fennel (to 4.61 +/- 1.26), while the placebo group showed minimal change (6.24 +/- 1.51). Ginger also led to the most significant reduction in pain intensity (mean difference: 0.74 +/- 0.61; P < 0.001) and duration (from 10.78 +/- 5.24 to 5.60 +/- 4.61 h/day; P < 0.001), outperforming both fennel and placebo. Statistical analyses confirmed significant between group differences (ANOVA F > 100, P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Both ginger and fennel significantly alleviated menstrual pain in terms of severity, intensity and duration, with ginger demonstrating superior therapeutic benefits. These findings underscore the clinical potential of herbal interventions as effective, safe and culturally acceptable alternatives for managing primary dysmenorrhea, particularly in low-resource settings. Integration of such plant-based therapies into routine menstrual health care may reduce reliance on conventional medications and improve quality of life among affected women.

   outcome measures; quality of life; type 2
AB BACKGROUND:Diabetes mellitus significantly impacts health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Data from urban primary care settings in South India remain limited. This study assessed HRQoL among type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) patients and identified demographic and clinical determinants associated with EuroQol five-dimension five level (EQ-5D-5L) index and EQ visual analogue scale (EQ-VAS) scores. MATERIALS AND METHODS:A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted (April-July 2025) at the urban health training center (UHTC), Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu, India. A total of 279 T2DM patients (aged >= 18 years) were enrolled using consecutive sampling. HRQoL was assessed using the licensed Tamil and English EQ-5D-5L questionnaire. Data were analyzed using R software; Chi-square tests and independent t-tests were applied (P < 0.05). RESULTS:Mean EQ-5D-5L index was 0.63 +/- 0.37 and EQ-VAS was 72.6 +/- 18.0. Pain/discomfort (52.1%) and anxiety/depression (43.2%) were the most affected dimensions. Microvascular complications (neuropathy P = 0.001; nephropathy P = 0.001; retinopathy P = 0.003), longer disease duration (P = 0.001), hospitalization (P = 0.001), and lower income (P = 0.003) were significantly associated with poorer HRQoL. CONCLUSION:Pain/discomfort and psychological distress are the most impaired HRQoL domains in urban South Indian T2DM patients. Microvascular complications, longer disease duration, hospitalization, and lower socioeconomic status are key determinants. These findings support integrating HRQoL monitoring within primary care non-communicable diseases (NCD) programmers under the National Programmed for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases and Stroke (NPCDCS) framework.

TI Effects of an online stroke education program on enhancing knowledge,
   awareness of stroke warning signs, and emergency medical services
   seeking among high-risk residents in Huanggang City, China

LA English
DT Article
DE Stroke; Emergency medical services; Awareness; Knowledge; Health belief
   model; Online education
AB BACKGROUND:Stroke is the leading cause of disability and death in china. Raising public awareness of warning signs is critical for improving access to emergency services and treatment outcomes. Prehospital delay remains a significant challenge, especially among high-risk populations. This study therefore aims to determine the effects of an online stroke education program (osp) on the knowledge, awareness of stroke warning signs, and seeking of emergency medical services (ems) among high-risk residents. MATERIALS AND METHODS:A randomized controlled trial was conducted from September 2024 to April 2025. One hundred and six high-risk residents were randomly allocated to intervention and control groups (n = 53 each). CONCLUSION:The OSP significantly improved stroke recognition and EMS-seeking intentions. Such integration is crucial for improving clinical outcomes in acute stroke management and achieving public health targets.

TI Management of acute pyelonephritis in pregnancy in emergency settings: A
   comparative study of conservative therapy and renal drainage
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Acute pyelonephritis; clinical decision-making; pregnancy; renal
   drainage; risk assessment; urinary tract
ID SYSTEMS
AB BACKGROUND: Acute pyelonephritis in pregnancy is a serious clinical condition requiring timely decision-making between conservative therapy and renal drainage. However, the absence of standardized objective criteria may result in delayed intervention and increased maternal morbidity. This study introduces and evaluates the clinical utility of a novel 10-parameter risk stratification scale designed to standardize treatment decisions in acute gestational pyelonephritis (AGP). MATERIALS AND METHODS: A single-center retrospective-prospective comparative observational study was conducted on 451 pregnant women with AGP between 2023 and 2025. Patients treated before (2023) and after (2024-2025) implementation of a 10-parameter risk stratification scale were compared. Statistical analysis included the Chi-square test, Mann-Whitney U test, and Spearman correlation, with significance set at P < 0.05. Where applicable, 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated. RESULTS: Implementation of the risk scale was associated with improved clinical outcomes. The success rate of conservative therapy increased by 2.7% (P < 0.05). The rate of ureteral stenting decreased from 13.8% to 9.7% (difference -4.1%; 95% CI: -7.8% to -0.4%). The mean decision-making time decreased from 24.3 +/- 6.1 hours to 12.8 +/- 4.2 hours (mean difference -11.8 hours; 95% CI: -13.5 to -10.1; P < 0.01). CONCLUSION: The 10-parameter risk assessment scale shows potential as a structured and objective framework, pending external validation for clinical decision-making in AGP. Its implementation is associated with reduced invasive interventions, improved efficiency in clinical decision-making, and better risk-based stratification of patients. However, findings should be interpreted with caution due to the single-center design, lack of multivariable adjustment, and absence of fetal outcomes.

TI Reframing astronomical observation as inference under measurement
   constraints: integrating interferometry and quantum sensing in the
   laboratory
SO EUROPEAN JOURNAL OF PHYSICS
LA English
DT Article
DE astronomical observation; interferometry; coherence; Michelson and
   Mach-Zehnder; optically detected magnetic resonance; nitrogen-vacancy
   centres; quantum sensing; measurement uncertainty
ID INFORMATION
AB School astronomy often frames observation as telescope-mediated seeing, whereas contemporary astronomy relies on phase-sensitive correlation, noise-limited signal extraction and model-based inference. We present a modular laboratory sequence for introductory optics and modern-physics laboratories that reframes observation as inference under measurement constraints through engineering-oriented tasks: (i) Michelson and Mach-Zehnder interferometry (alignment, stabilisation, fringe loss and recovery), (ii) polarisation investigations emphasising configuration-dependent information, and (iii) nitrogen-vacancy centre optically detected magnetic resonance for magnetic-field inference via spectral features. The stations can be implemented as qualitative 'make-it-work' measurement systems or extended to quantitative analysis (e.g. fringe visibility metrics, Jones/Stokes modelling, Lorentzian fitting with uncertainty propagation). In a pilot implementation with a bridging cohort (single-group pre-post design; N = 66, matched n = 59), scores on the 16-item Astronomical Measurement Limits Survey (AMLS) increased from M = 3.98 (SD = 0.47) to M = 4.41 (SD = 0.46), consistent with a large within-group effect ( dz approximate to 1.0). Performance on four aligned concept items increased from a mean proportion correct of 0.62 (SD = 0.28) to 0.78 (SD = 0.25). Given the absence of a comparison group and immediate post-testing, findings are interpreted as formative evidence of short-term shifts toward measurement-limited reasoning rather than as causal estimates. Instructor notes, assessment materials and analysis code are provided to support replication and further evaluation.

TI The effect of peer-assisted learning on medication error occurrence
   among undergraduate nursing students: A randomized controlled trial
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Medication error; nursing student; peer teaching; peer-assistance
   learning
AB BACKGROUND: Medication administration is one of the most sensitive duties of nurses and an essential part of the treatment and care process. Nursing students are more likely to make medication errors because of their inexperience and lack of ability. The importance of clinical education using modern approaches is undeniable. This study was conducted to investigate the effect of peer-assisted learning on medication error occurrence among undergraduate nursing students. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study is a randomized controlled trial, conducted in 2023-24, involving 50 fourth-semester undergraduate nursing students at a nursing school in Tehran, Iran. Students were chosen through a census method, and randomly divided into intervention and control groups. The intervention group was taught pharmacotherapy via peer teaching, and data were collected using the Medication Error Occurrence Questionnaire (MEOQ). The data analysis was performed using SPSS software, and descriptive statistical tests such as mean, SD, frequency, and percentage were employed. Several other statistical tests were utilized, including Fisher's exact test, Chi-squared test, independent t-test, and paired t-test. RESULTS: Before the intervention, there were no significant differences in medication error occurrence between the intervention and control groups (P > 0.05). Upon utilizing peer teaching, the intervention group exhibited significant reductions in medication error occurrence, from 65.76 +/- 9.75 to 56.76 +/- 13.69 (P = 0.001). In contrast, the control group experienced a slight reduce in medication error occurrence level, from 68.32 +/- 12.41 to 66.28 +/- 18.94 (P = 0.276). CONCLUSION: Peer teaching significantly reduced nursing students' medication error occurrence, recommending its adoption as an innovative educational method. It is recommended that the peer method be used to improve the clinical education of nursing students.

   satisfaction in reproductive-age women: A cross-sectional study in Iran

LA English
DT Article
DE Body mass index; marital satisfaction; obesity; sexual function; women
ID OBESE WOMEN; DYSFUNCTION; RISK; OVERWEIGHT; HEALTH; LIFE
AB BACKGROUND: Obesity is a global issue and has negative effects on various aspects of life, including physical and psychosocial health, which leads to a reduced quality of life. The present study was conducted to investigate the relationships between body mass index, sexual function, and marital satisfaction in reproductive-aged women. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The present research was a cross-sectional study that was conducted using socio-demographic and obstetric checklist, and questionnaires, including the Female Sexual Function Inventory (FSFI) and Enrich Marital satisfaction questionnaire as well as using a weight scale and stadiometer to measure height on 350 women of reproductive age referred to health centers during 2022 in Babol, Iran. TI Effectiveness of coping strategies regarding fear of missing out on
   academic performance among nursing and pharmacy students at selected
   colleges, Coimbatore, India
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Academic performance; coping strategies; fear of missing out; nursing
   students; pharmacy students
AB BACKGROUND: Fear of missing out (FoMO) is a pervasive concern in the digital age, particularly among healthcare students, potentially impairing academic engagement and performance. There is a need for evidence-based interventions to mitigate FoMO in high-pressure educational settings such as nursing and pharmacy. METHODS AND MATERIAL: A pre-test-post-test comparative experimental study was conducted in 2024 among 120 nursing and pharmacy students (aged 20-22 years) selected via stratified random sampling and randomly assigned to intervention (n = 60) or routine care (n = 60) groups. The intervention consisted of five one-hour sessions on coping strategies (seeking support, time management, goal setting, stress reduction, and balanced lifestyle). FoMO was measured using the Fear of Missing Out Scale (FoMOS), and academic performance was assessed via the Situated Academic Writing Self-Efficacy Scale (SAWSES). Data were analyzed using SPSS v28.0 with paired and unpaired t-tests and correlation analyses. RESULTS: Significant reductions in FoMO scores were observed in the intervention group compared to controls (nursing: t = 3.82, P = 0.05; pharmacy: t = 4.43, P = 0.037). Academic writing self-efficacy improved significantly in the intervention group (P < 0.05). A strong positive correlation was found between pre-test and post-test FoMO (r = 0.401, P < 0.01) and academic performance (r = 0.691, P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: The structured coping strategies intervention significantly reduced FoMO and enhanced academic writing self-efficacy among nursing and pharmacy students. Integrating such programs into student support services is recommended to promote academic well-being.

TI Inflammatory indices and bone density in osteoporosis: A cross-sectional
   study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Bone density; inflammation; neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio;
   osteoporosis; platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio
ID DIFFERENCE; HEALTH
AB BACKGROUND: Osteoporosis and osteopenia, prevalent metabolic bone disorders, increase fracture risk, particularly in postmenopausal women. Chronic inflammation may contribute to bone loss. The association between inflammatory indices and bone mineral density (BMD) was investigated. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional analysis involving 99 patients over the age of 40 at the Ilam Rheumatology Clinic (2019-2022) evaluated BMD using the Hologic Discovery Wi DXA and assessed blood indices with the Sysmex XN-1000. Statistical analyses, including T-tests, ANOVA, and Pearson's correlation, were conducted utilizing SPSS version 16, with significance set at P < 0.05. RESULTS: Among 99 patients (78.8% female, mean age 55.8 +/- 9.7 years), the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) exhibited significant elevation in cases of osteoporosis (2.710 +/- 0.610, P = 0.001) and osteopenia (2.230 +/- 0.530, P = 0.001) than in normal BMD (1.840 +/- 0.450). The BMD exhibited a negative correlation with the NLR (r = -0.430, P = 0.001) and the PLR (r = -0.370, P = 0.002). Patients with osteoporosis exhibited the lowest bone mineral density in the lumbar spine (P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Increased levels of NLR and PLR correlate with diminished BMD, suggesting their potential as cost-effective biomarkers for osteoporosis risk assessment. Monitoring these indices could enhance early diagnosis and prevention strategies in at-risk populations.

TI Impact of burden of care upon psychological wellbeing and quality of
   life among family caregivers for cancer patients
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Burden of care; cancer; family caregivers; psychological distress;
   psychological wellbeing; quality of life
AB BACKGROUND:Cancer is a serious and fatal disease that affects both the patients themselves and their families. This study aimed to investigate the impact of caregiving burden on the quality of life and mental health of family caregivers of cancer patients. MATERIALS AND METHODS:This research is a cross-sectional study that further investigates family caregivers for their patients with cancer at babel oncology Center in Babylon, Iraq, from September 2025 to February 2026. A purposive sampling method that was applied to a group of 150 patients. Information was gathered through self-report questionnaire. SPSS version 26 was utilized to analyze the data. RESULTS:The results showed that 73.3% of caregivers had a poor caregiving burden and 24.7% had a moderate caregiving burden, with approximately 74% having a fair quality of life, while 52.7% of caregivers had a good level of psychological well-being. The analyses also revealed a statistically significant relationship between caregiving burden and quality of life, and a statistically significant inverse relationship between caregiving burden and psychological well-being (P < 0.001). CONCLUSION:The majority of caregivers have a low caregiving burden and a fair level of quality of life, and approximately half have a good level of psychological well-being. The results also showed a relationship between burden and quality of life; any change in burden level was accompanied by a change in quality of life. Furthermore, there is a significant inverse relationship between burden and psychological well-being.

TI Artificial intelligence and its impact on oral health care education. A
   randomized study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Artificial intelligence; awareness; health education; oral health; oral
   hygiene; rural
AB BACKGROUND:Artificial intelligence (AI)-generated educational materials demonstrate superior effectiveness in improving patient comprehension and reducing anxiety compared to traditional methods. Their integration into dental practice could enhance patient satisfaction and streamline the educational process, particularly for complex or anxiety-inducing procedures. The present study aimed to evaluate the act of AI applications on oral healthcare, focusing on clinical outcomes. MATERIALS AND METHODS:A cluster-randomized controlled trial with 1000 participants from 20 villages (10 interventions, 10 controls) was conducted. The intervention group received 4 weeks of chatbot-guided oral health education via WhatsApp/IVR, while controls received standard health talks and leaflets. Knowledge, oral hygiene practices, and OHI-S scores were measured pre- and post-intervention. RESULTS:The intervention group showed a marked rise in mean knowledge scores (9.8 to 15.2) compared to controls (10.1 to 11.3; P < 0.001). Twice-daily brushing improved from 28% to 64% (vs. 30% to 37% in controls). OHI-S scores improved significantly more in the chatbot group (reduction = 1.2) than in controls (0.3; P < 0.001). Engagement with the chatbot correlated positively with outcome improvements. CONCLUSION:AI-based chatbots significantly enhance oral health awareness, hygiene practices, and clinical outcomes in rural settings, highlighting their potential for scalable public health interventions and integration into primary health programs.

TI Can spiritual care education reduce the anxiety of mothers of
   hospitalized immature infants?
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Maternal anxiety; neonatal intensive care unit; spirituality
AB BACKGROUND: Hospitalization of a preterm infant in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) is a significant stressor for mothers, often leading to heightened anxiety that affects both their well-being and maternal-infant interaction. Spiritual self-care is a nonpharmacological approach that can help mothers manage anxiety and cope with their child's hospitalization. This study examines the impact of spiritual self-care education on maternal anxiety in mothers with preterm infants admitted to the NICU. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This quasi-experimental study involved 90 mothers of preterm infants, selected through convenience sampling and randomly assigned to control (n = 45) and intervention (n = 45) groups. The intervention consisted of five 45-min spiritual self-care training sessions held every other day. Participants provided written informed consent, and data were collected using a demographic questionnaire and the Beck Anxiety Inventory (21 items). > Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 27. The software was developed by IBM Corp., located in Armonk, New York, United States, applying t-tests, Chi-square tests, and analysis of variance. RESULTS: The mean maternal age was 32.4 +/- 5.7 years in the intervention group and 33 +/- 6.06 years in the control group (P < 0.05). The mean birth weight was lower in the intervention group (2063.1 +/- 460.98 g vs. 2278 +/- 275.57 g, P < 0.05). Anxiety scores decreased significantly post-intervention in both groups (P < 0.001), with a greater reduction observed in the intervention group. CONCLUSION: Spiritual self-care education significantly reduces anxiety in mothers of preterm infants, suggesting its usefulness for healthcare providers. Future research should explore how best to integrate spiritual self-care education into standard NICU care and investigate its impact on long-term maternal mental health outcomes.
