TI Sawdust-plaster cast mixture versus traditional cast: Which type reduced
   pain and increases comfort and enhancing healing process among patients
   with twisting: A randomized controlled clinical trial
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Comfort; healing; pain; plaster cast; randomized trial; sawdust;
   traditional cast; twisting injuries
AB BACKGROUND: Musculoskeletal twisting injuries, such as strains and sprains, are common and can be treated using cast immobilization without the need for surgery. The study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of Sawdust-Plaster Cast Mixture Versus Traditional Cast: Which Type Reduced Pain and Increases Comfort and Enhancing the healing process among Patients with Twisting. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The study was conducted from May to August 2025 and used a single-blind, true experimental design. Sixty patients with twisting injuries were randomly assigned to either the intervention group (n = 29), which received the sawdust-plaster cast, or the control group (n = 31), which received a standard cast. Pain and comfort levels were assessed using a visual analog scale (VAS), and the healing duration was recorded. Statistical analysis was performed using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) version 30. RESULTS: Compared to the standard cast (control) group, patients in the sawdust-plaster cast mixture (intervention) group reported a noticeably higher reduction in discomfort. The intervention group's mean pain score was 18.37 (P < 0.001), compared to 43.47 for the control group. Enhanced Comfort: Additionally, the intervention group reported feeling much more at ease. The intervention group's mean comfort score was 24.40 (P = 0.003), while the control group's was 36.21. For the sawdust-plaster cast mixture group, the healing period was noticeably shorter. The intervention group's mean recovery time was 25.11 days (P = 0.004), compared to 36.26 days for the control group. CONCLUSION: The intervention showed a notable and clinically significant improvement in patient outcomes based on health policy criteria. This directly addressed important health policy goals for enhancing patient experience and care quality. Additionally, the average healing time decreased by more than 30% (36.26-25.11 days), demonstrating the effectiveness of the intervention in hastening patient recuperation and enhancing productivity. These results show that the intervention not only satisfies but also exceeds standards for efficient, patient-centered care.

TI A neuroeducational approach to STEM education: Integrating real-time
   cognitive analysis and cognitive load theory to optimize teaching and
   learning at universities
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Cognitive Load; Neuro-education; Adaptive Learning; Cognitive Analysis;
   STEM Education
AB BACKGROUND:The relevance of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education to effectively meet challenging academic requirements has become imperative for university entrants. With emerging advancements within the domain of learning neuroscience and analytics, it has become possible to analyze and track the real-time mental states of learners. This has opened several avenues to apply the theoretical perspectives of Cognitive Load Theory (CLT). Though applications of neuro-technological interventions for learning have become widely sought, their effective implementation within STEM education has not been comprehensive at the university level. The innovations brought about within this study include its conceptual fusion for STEM education based upon real-time mental state analysis and CLT. The goal of this research is to integrate the current research findings on real-time cognitive analysis practices used in STEM education in universities and analyze how cognitive load can be monitored dynamically and discuss teaching practices according to principles of CLT to improve effectiveness and inclusiveness for better cognitive load management throughout learning. MATERIALS AND METHODS:A systematic narrative review with cross-case synthesis was conducted using peer-reviewed empirical studies published between 2018 and 2025. The relevant articles were identified through the searching of databases such as Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, and PsycINFO. Studies focusing on higher education STEM contexts were included if they employed neuroeducational tools (e.g., electroencephalography, functional near-infrared spectroscopy, eye tracking, or artificial intelligence-driven analytics) or incorporated instructional designs informed by Cognitive Load Theory (CLT). A standardized framework for extracting data was used, and data were thematically analyzed to identify patterns across the studies regarding cognitive load measurement, adaptive instructional strategies, learning outcomes, teacher experiences, and ethical considerations. RESULTS:From the synthesis, real-time cognitive feedback is perceived to have positively influenced teaching effectiveness by allowing the instructor to dynamically adjust pacing, scaffolding, and learning activities (d = 0.68-0.72, P < 0.01). Multimodal cognitive analytics were also associated with more precise estimates of cognitive load, supporting the development of adaptive learning strategies. It is also apparent that cognitively based personalization is effective in reducing the cognitive load and improving motivation and knowledge acquisition for both diverse and neurodiverse students. CONCLUSION:The synergistic combination of real-time cognitive analysis and CLT has the potential for making progressive inroads for inclusive and adaptive STEM education in universities. This conceptual combination is in good harmony with the benchmarks for health and educational policy that regard evidence-based instruction, the welfare of the learner, and equity in higher educational settings as cornerstones. Longitudinal study, ethical regulation, and implementation strategies for neuroeducational data in universities need more emphasis in future studies.

TI Design and validation of a multisensory game-based tooth brushing
   education tool for children with visual and hearing impairment
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Games; learning; hearing loss; health education; oral hygiene; sensory
   disorders; toothbrushing; vision disorders
AB BACKGROUND: Children with sensory disabilities exhibit a poor oral hygiene and a high prevalence of gingivitis and dental caries. Tailored multisensory oral health education interventions may improve tooth brushing skills and oral health. To develop and validate a multisensory game-based educational intervention to teach tooth brushing to children with visual and hearing impairments. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A developmental research design was used. A prototype was developed after literature review and expert interviews. This was validated by dentists and special educators and field tested among 15 children with visual impairment and 15 with hearing impairment with 7 play sessions over 4 weeks. Comprehensibility and acceptability were assessed through structured feedback, and effectiveness was measured by evaluating tooth brushing skills. RESULTS: Experts agreed with the relevance, sequential accuracy of the brushing technique, and clarity of the game (Item-level Content Validity Index (I-CVI) and k* =1.00), confirming excellent content validity. Dentists suggested minor modifications regarding sequencing flexibility and a special educator suggested audio/light cues. Children with visual impairment rated the game and the tooth brushing technique as easy to understand and the components easy to handle (I-CVI = 1.00), enjoyable (I-CVI = 0.93), and some suggested larger models. Children with hearing impairment showed perfect agreement across all aspects of the game. The children showed improvements in their tooth brushing skills (W = 0.00, P < 0.05). CONCLUSION: The developed game-based educational intervention demonstrates strong validity and acceptability for oral hygiene education among children with sensory impairments. These findings support further evaluation of long-term effectiveness and application in oral health promotion.

TI Effectiveness of video-enhanced educational intervention for fluid
   management on knowledge, practice, and adherence among patients
   undergoing hemodialysis: A randomized controlled trial
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Attitude; practice; fluid restriction; health knowledge; kidney failure;
   patient compliance; renal dialysis; video-aided instruction
ID SELF-MANAGEMENT; CONSEQUENCES
AB BACKGROUND:Fluid management remains a cornerstone of hemodialysis care; however, suboptimal adherence frequently precipitates life-threatening complications, including hypertension and cardiovascular morbidity. While educational interventions are essential to mitigate these risks, empirical evidence regarding the efficacy of video-enhanced instruction in this population remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of a structured video-enhanced educational intervention on knowledge, practice, and fluid adherence among patients undergoing hemodialysis. MATERIALS AND METHODS:This randomized controlled trial evaluated outcomes using a knowledge questionnaire (reliability 0.88), a practice checklist (0.79), and intradialytic weight gain (IDWG) in 128 hemodialysis patients at South Indian tertiary hospital. Participants (n = 64 per experimental and control group, block randomized) received video-enhanced fluid management education or standard care; analysis included t-test, repeated measures of ANOVA, and Bonferroni tests (P < 0.05 significant). RESULTS:The experimental group showed significant improvements in mean knowledge scores (11.4 +/- 2.2) vs control, P = 0.001) and practice scores (13.6 +/- 1.0 vs control 9.1 +/- 1.5, P = 0.001) from pretest to post-test 2. Repeated measures ANOVA confirmed differences in practice scores within (F = 102.76, P = 0.001) and between groups (F = 8121.19, P = 0.001), with fluid adherence also improving significantly in the experimental group (P < 0.001). CONCLUSION:Video-enhanced instruction is an effective strategy to improve clinical outcomes in hemodialysis patients. Integrating a structured audiovisual tool into routine dialysis care can enhance patient outcomes and support healthcare policy initiatives to improve chronic disease management.

TI Navigating the storm: A qualitative research on contributing factors to
   diabetes burnout in young adults with type 1 diabetes
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Burnout; chronic disease; diabetes mellitus; disease management;
   psychological; qualitative research; type 1; young adults
ID MODEL
AB BACKGROUND:Diabetes burnout is a serious and often overlooked condition marked by emotional exhaustion, detachment, and a sense of helplessness in managing diabetes. This qualitative content analysis study seeks to uncover the underlying factors that contribute to the onset and persistence of diabetes burnout. Understanding these factors is essential for informing targeted interventions and supportive policies to improve the well-being of individuals living with Type 1 diabetes.MATERIALS AND METHODS:Eleven adults with T1D in Shahrekord, Iran, were recruited using purposive sampling to ensure diverse perspectives. Fourteen semi-structured interviews (50-60 minutes each) were conducted in Persian, with two participants completing follow-up sessions. Interviews were recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using Elo and Kyng & auml;s's three-step process: open coding, categorization, and abstraction. Trustworthiness was ensured through prolonged engagement, peer debriefing, member checking, and application of Lincoln and Guba's criteria.RESULTS:Qualitative analysis revealed four interrelated themes contributing to burnout: (1) disruptions in self-management routines (e.g., sleep, exercise, diet); (2) external stressors and resource limitations (e.g., economic instability, healthcare access, medication shortages); (3) fluctuations in physical and emotional well-being; and (4) the role of interpersonal and social support. Many of these challenges were exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, which disrupted healthcare routines and increased psychosocial stress. Participants likened their experience to navigating a suspension bridge-requiring constant adaptation amid instability. These findings highlight the need for holistic diabetes care that addresses both medical and social dimensions, especially during times of crisis.CONCLUSION:This study reveals diabetes burnout as a critical but often overlooked barrier to effective diabetes management. Disruptions in daily routines, compounded by crises, heighten burnout risks. Aligning with global health policy benchmarks, our findings support the need for integrated care that addresses both medical and psychosocial aspects of diabetes. Health systems should prioritize mental health support, routine stability, and access to essential resources to improve long-term outcomes for people with type 1 diabetes.

TI The impact of group cognitive behavioral therapy on stress and
   psychological adjustment among cigarette, e-cigarette, and hookah
   smokers
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Cigarette; cognitive behavioral therapy; e-cigarette; hookah;
   psychological adjustment; psychological stress
ID TOBACCO PRODUCT USE; UNITED-STATES; STUDENTS; SMOKING; VALUES; YOUTH
AB BACKGROUND:The tobacco epidemic remains one of the world's major public health threats, causing preventable cancers and disabilities, and claiming over seven million lives each year. Over the past decade, the use of nicotine-containing electronic cigarettes has grown among adolescents and young adults. This study investigates the effectiveness of a group cognitive behavioral therapy program on stress and psychological adjustment among university students who want to quit smoking cigarettes or hookah.MATERIALS AND METHODS:The sample included 123 male students who smoked cigarettes and e-cigarettes and 134 students who smoked hookah, all of whom expressed a desire to quit smoking. Students who smoke both cigarettes and hookah were excluded from the study to ensure clear differentiation between the two groups of users. A nonprobability sampling method was used. Psychological stress and psychological adjustments were measured twice: before the group treatment program began and after the program was completed. The study employed an experimental pretest and posttest design to analyze data.RESULTS:The results indicated that the program had an effective impact on users of cigarettes, electronic cigarettes, and hookah in terms of stress management strategies and psychological adjustment. Specifically, the program had a positive effect on reducing psychological stress but a negative effect on psychological adjustment, meaning that while stress levels decreased, psychological adjustment also decreased. The program had a greater impact on stress management strategies and psychological adjustment among cigarette and e-cigarette smokers compared to hookah smokers.CONCLUSION:The findings suggest that smokers of cigarettes and e-cigarettes are more likely to use stress-coping strategies but have a reduced ability to maintain psychological adjustment, which may be due to their dependence on nicotine. Therefore, it is recommended that awareness be raised about the necessity of involving psychologists in future treatment programs at the national level to help reduce this phenomenon.

TI Spiritual well-being, sleep quality as a buffer against burnout and in
   increasing professional fulfillment among healthcare professionals in
   the United Arab Emirates
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Burnout; occupational health; professional fulfilment; sleep
   disturbance; sleep quality; spiritual well-being
ID MENTAL-HEALTH; STRESS; NURSES; PHYSICIANS
AB BACKGROUND:Burnout is a growing concern among healthcare professionals (HCPs) in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Emerging evidence suggests that sleep quality and spiritual well-being may buffer against burnout and enhance professional fulfilment. This study explores the relationship between sleep disturbance, spiritual well-being, and burnout among HCPs in the UAE.MATERIALS AND METHODS:A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 661 healthcare professionals across the UAE. Validated instruments were used to measure sleep quality, circadian regularity, spiritual well-being, burnout, and professional fulfilment. Data was analyzed using correlation and regression models to identify predictive factors.RESULTS:Poor sleep quality and irregular circadian patterns were significantly associated with higher levels of burnout. Conversely, higher spiritual well-being showed a strong negative correlation with burnout and a positive association with professional fulfilment. Multivariate analysis identified sleep regularity and spiritual well-being as significant independent predictors of both burnout and professional fulfilment.CONCLUSION:Sleep quality and spiritual well-being play a protective role against burnout and contribute to greater professional fulfilment among healthcare professionals in the UAE. These findings highlight the importance of addressing sleep issues and nurturing spiritual well-being to mitigate burnout and enhance job satisfaction among healthcare professionals, thereby facilitating targeted interventions for improved occupational health and well-being.

TI A true experimental study to assess the effectiveness of holistic
   self-care approach on clinical parameters, psychological stress,
   wellbeing, among antenatal mothers with pregnancy-induced hypertension
   admitted in antenatal ward at SRM Medical College Hospital and Research
   Centre
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Antenatal mothers; clinical parameters; holistic self-care approach;
   Mitchell's relaxation; pregnancy-induced hypertension; psychological
   stress; wellbeing
ID DISEASES; RISK
AB BACKGROUND:Pregnancy-related hypertension diseases are a global concern. Pregnancy-induced hypertensive problems affect 5-8% of pregnant women worldwide. Maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality are primarily caused by pre-eclampsia and eclampsia. Five to seven percent of pregnancies end in pre-eclampsia, which manifests as proteinuria and hypertension.MATERIALS AND METHODS:A study with a pretest-posttest control group design was conducted among 80 antenatal mothers (40 control and 40 experimental) with pregnancy-induced hypertension (PIH) at SRM Medical College Hospital and Research Centre. The intervention included education on dietary changes, walking, leg and foot exercises, awareness of PIH warning signs, and Mitchell's relaxation techniques, administered for 7 consecutive days. Clinical parameters, stress (Perceived Stress Scale), and wellbeing (WEMWBS) were measured before and after the intervention.RESULTS:In the experimental group, stress scores slightly decreased (39.80 to 39.30; P = 0.096) and wellbeing modestly improved (44.53 to 45.33; P = 0.104). Significant reductions were noted in clinical parameters post intervention. Systolic BP dropped from 126.85 to 117.13 mmHg, and diastolic BP from 81.90 to 73.25 mmHg (P = 0.000). The pulse rate decreased from 90.28 to 75.80 bpm, and the respiratory rate from 21.49 to 19.05 (P = 0.000). This suggests the holistic self-care approach effectively improved clinical outcomes in PIH mothers.CONCLUSION:A holistic self-care approach significantly improved clinical parameters and psychological wellbeing in antenatal mothers with PIH, with reduced vital signs and stress levels in the intervention group.

TI Comparing the pain relief effectiveness of intravenous magnesium sulfate
   and ketorolac versus intravenous morphine and ketorolac for kidney
   stones
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Ketorolac; kidney calculi; magnesium sulfate; morphine; pain
AB BACKGROUND:Pain is one of the most common symptoms in various diseases. While morphine is widely used for pain relief, its adverse effects and potential for misuse have led to the exploration of safer alternatives. This study aimed to compare the analgesic effectiveness of intravenous magnesium sulfate versus morphine, both in combination with ketorolac, in patients with renal colic.MATERIALS AND METHODS:In this double-blind randomized controlled trial, 174 patients with renal colic referred to the emergency department of Shahid Ganjiyan Hospital in Dezful were enrolled. Patients were randomly allocated into two equal groups (n = 87). The intervention group received intravenous magnesium sulfate (50 mg/kg diluted in 100 mL normal saline over 15 minutes) plus ketorolac (30 mg), while the control group received intravenous morphine (0.1 mg/kg) plus ketorolac (30 mg). Pain intensity was measured using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) at baseline (admission), and 20, 40, and 60 minutes after drug administration. Demographic data were also collected.RESULT:Among the 174 participants included in the study, 65% were male and aged between 40 and 60 years. Statistical tests indicated no significant differences between the two groups concerning demographic characteristics. Thus, the groups are comparable in terms of demographic variables. Comparison of pain reduction between the two groups at different time points revealed no statistically significant difference. The mean pain scores decreased over time in both groups; however, the differences between the groups were not significant at 20 minutes (P = 0.45), 40 minutes (P = 0.74), or 60 minutes post-intervention (P = 0.65). These findings indicate that both treatment protocols (morphine plus ketorolac and magnesium sulfate plus ketorolac) had similar effects on pain reduction at all measured intervals.CONCLUSION:The findings of this study demonstrate that intravenous magnesium sulfate, in combination with ketorolac, is as effective as morphine-based regimens in managing acute renal colic pain. Given the current global health policies emphasizing opioid stewardship and the reduction of opioid-related adverse effects, magnesium sulfate emerges as a valuable, low-risk alternative. Its incorporation into emergency pain management protocols may not only reduce opioid dependency and misuse but also align with broader public health goals aimed at promoting safer and more sustainable pain relief strategies. Health policymakers should consider including non-opioid analgesics like magnesium sulfate in national and institutional guidelines for acute pain management, especially in settings where opioid overuse presents a clinical and social challenge.

TI Determinant factors of sexual and reproductive health literacy among
   adolescents in Indonesia: A national population-based study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Adolescents; health; literacy; reproductive; sexual
ID INTERVENTIONS; EDUCATION; SCHOOL; MEDIA
AB BACKGROUND:Sexual and reproductive health literacy (SRHL) among adolescents is a global public health concern. Almost half of all new cases of sexually transmitted infections have been associated with health literacy among youth. Limited SRHL has led to negative behaviours and their impact on health-related outcomes. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to identify the determinants of SRHL among adolescents in Indonesia.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This study drew on the most recent nationwide, population-based cross-sectional study and applied Nutbeam's functional health literacy framework. SRHL was determined as a composite index and classified into three levels: limited, inadequate, and adequate. Pearson's Chi-square test was used to determine the different proportions of SRHL. Binary logistic regression with a complex survey design was used to evaluate the factors associated with SRHL. The crude and adjusted odds ratios (AOR) along with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were reported.RESULTS:The magnitude of adequate literacy was 32.69% (95% CI, 31.92%-33.45%). Adolescents with advanced understanding and awareness of family function (AOR: 3.98; 3.36-4.72), female (AOR: 3.41; 2.90-4.02), internet usage (AOR: 3.07; 2.49-3.79), higher education (AOR: 2.96; 2.20-3.98), and dating experience (AOR: 2.52; 1.81-3.50) were associated with adequate SRHL in Indonesia. Moreover, parental knowledge (AOR: 2.03; 1.63-2.53), optimal information access (AOR: 2.35; 2.01-2.75), and liberal attitude toward early marriage (AOR: 2.16; 1.86-2.50) were more likely to have adequate literacy.CONCLUSION:Comprehensive public health strategies, including integrating reproductive health education, strengthening parental communication, and leveraging digital media were suggested to improve adolescent's health literacy.

TI Exploring the convergence of faith healing practices with
   biopsychosocial interventions for mental health: A qualitative study
   among faith healers in Madhya Pradesh, India
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Faith healer; health-seeking behavior; India; integration; mental
   health; psychiatric care; stigma; superstition; traditional healer
ID ILLNESS; CARE
AB BACKGROUND:Faith healing, a practice deeply rooted in cultural and religious beliefs, remains a significant healthcare approach worldwide, especially in regions like India, where mental health stigma is pervasive. Despite advances in psychiatric care, many individuals still seek the services of faith healers for mental health issues, delaying access to appropriate medical treatment. The study aims to understand the perspectives of Faith Healers on mental health, examine their practices and beliefs, and explore the feasibility of integrating faith healing with psychiatric care to enhance mental health outcomes in Madhya Pradesh.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This qualitative study was conducted across selected districts of Madhya Pradesh, India. The participants were Faith Healers' who were interviewed by Psychiatrists from "Mankaksh" (District Mental Health Units) between July 2022 and February 2023. In-depth interviews (IDIs) were conducted with 24 faith healers using a predefined interview guide. These IDIs were later analyzed. Thematic analysis was used to identify key themes from the data.RESULTS:The following four themes emerged: Reason for working in the profession, Perception regarding issues of disciples, View on integration of Faith healing and Psychiatric treatment, and Interventions suggested. Opinions on integrating faith healing with psychiatric care varied, with some expressing openness to collaboration, while others remained skeptical of medical interventions.CONCLUSIONS:The study highlights the complex relationship between faith healing and mental health care in Madhya Pradesh. Collaboration between faith healers and mental health practitioners is essential for developing holistic care models that respect cultural beliefs while ensuring evidence-based treatment.

TI Localizing the main components of competencies in high-level managers
   based on health system evaluation indicators: Content analysis approach
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Competence; health education; health promotion; high-level managers;
   University of Medical Sciences
ID OCCUPATIONAL-HEALTH; JOB-SATISFACTION; SAFETY; NURSES
AB BACKGROUND:Managers play a key role in organizations. Competence of managers has become an important issue for organizations. This issue is very important for high-level managers in health-oriented organizations. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to identify and determine the components and analyze the core competencies of high-level managers in the field of health in medical sciences universities of the country, with the approach of content analysis.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This qualitative study was conducted using the content analysis method in 2023-2024. Data collection included retrieving documents from relevant databases. The studied population was high-level managers in the field of health promotion (presidents, vice presidents, university professors, and experienced human resource managers). For this purpose, semi-structured interviews were conducted with managers. The purposeful sampling method was chosen, and finally, the sampling was continued until the saturation time. The interview text was analyzed and the opinions of experts were included to extract key concepts and categorize them into main topics using 12 MAXQDA software. Finally, the Delphi technique was used to determine the components of the main competencies of high-level managers of Iranian medical sciences universities.FINDINGS:In this study, after analyzing the content of the interviews, 5 dimensions of the main components, including managerial competencies, perceptual competencies, personality (individual) competencies, communication competencies, and moral competencies were determined. Also, the results of MAXQDA software identified 30 components for 5 dimensions.CONCLUSION:Considering the key role of universities in the development of various ecosystems, it is considered very important to pay attention to the competencies of managers who are at the top of decision-making in medical sciences universities. Identifying, localizing, and determining the main and core components of competencies in high-level managers can be used as a tool to select health system managers based on these competencies. This choice can take steps towards improving the level of health and health education and adopting appropriate health policies in this field, the efficiency of the health system and the quality effectiveness of the management of medical sciences universities.

TI Navigating the PhD thesis journey: A qualitative study of doctoral
   students and supervisors at a medical university in Iran
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Doctoral supervision; higher education; institutional reform; PhD
   thesis; qualitative research; student well-being
AB BACKGROUND:The PhD thesis serves as a cornerstone of doctoral education, yet it is often accompanied by considerable stress and inefficiencies for both students and supervisors. Although global research has extensively addressed issues such as supervision quality, institutional support, and student well-being, there is limited investigation into these dynamics from a qualitative perspective in non-Western academic settings. This study examines the lived experiences of doctoral students and their supervisors at Isfahan University of Medical Sciences to identify challenges and propose tailored reforms for this specific context.MATERIALS AND METHODS:Employing a qualitative exploratory design, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 54 participants (31 PhD students and 23 faculty supervisors) chosen through purposive sampling. The collected data underwent conventional content analysis, with themes integrated across both groups to form a unified framework.RESULTS:The analysis revealed five overarching themes and 21 associated categories, including supervisory competencies, administrative ambiguity, resource limitations, psychological stress, and the importance of early research engagement. While students stressed the need for emotional support and resource availability, supervisors emphasized clearer regulations and opportunities for professional development. Both groups underscored the necessity of fostering a supportive academic environment.CONCLUSION:The PhD thesis process operates as a dynamic system influenced by interpersonal relationships, institutional frameworks, and procedural clarity. Efforts to reform this process should prioritize supervisor training programs, simplified administrative procedures, enhanced resource availability, and comprehensive psychological support embedded throughout the doctoral journey.

TI Disparities in educational service quality among medical students in
   Iran's revised medical curriculum: A cross-sectional study in a
   resource-limited region
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Accreditation; education; equality; medical students; medically
   underserved area; quality assurance; social accountability; surveys and
   questionnaires
AB BACKGROUND:Ongoing evaluation of educational service quality in medical schools is essential, particularly in settings with limited resources. This study assessed the discrepancy between expected and perceived educational service quality among medical students in the Sistan region of Iran.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This cross-sectional analytical study involved 195 medical students enrolled in the revised curriculum at Zabol University of Medical Sciences. Data were collected using a demographic questionnaire and the SERVQUAL instrument, which measures the quality of educational services. Statistical analyses included paired t-tests, independent t-tests, and one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA).RESULTS:Significant negative gaps were found across all dimensions of educational service quality. The smallest discrepancy was identified in the tangibles domain, while the reliability domain showed the most significant gap. Non-local students reported greater dissatisfaction in the tangibles domain. Those planning to pursue postgraduate education expressed significantly larger gaps in both reliability and tangibles, as well as in overall service quality. Students in the physiopathology phase reported broader gaps compared to peers in the basic sciences and clinical clerkship stages.CONCLUSION:Educational service quality fell short of student expectations across all assessed domains. Addressing these gaps-especially in under-resourced environments-is vital to aligning educational services with student needs and strengthening their role as key stakeholders in medical training.

TI Women's outcome instrument for maternal health care (WOICE) of Iranian
   pregnant women after 35: A cross-sectional study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Advanced maternal age; maternal health; prenatal care
ID VALIDITY; ANXIETY; VERSION
AB BACKGROUND:Exploring the health dimensions of pregnant women over 35 opens a window into a deeper understanding of the physical and psychological challenges of this critical period and paves the way for targeted interventions. This study aimed to make the voices of pregnant women aged 35 and older heard.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This study was conducted in 2024 at three major hospitals in Tehran. We utilized the women's outcome instrument for maternal health care instrument, which was developed by the World Health Organization (WHO). TI A digital-spiritual assistance Dzikry model to improve hemoglobin levels
   and antenatal care compliance: A quasi-experimental study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Anemia; antenatal care; hemoglobin; mHealth; pregnancy; primary health
   care; spirituality
ID ANEMIA
AB BACKGROUND:Maternal anemia remains a significant contributor to adverse pregnancy outcomes, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Although universal health insurance has expanded access to antenatal care (ANC), coverage alone does not guarantee optimal utilization. Innovative approaches addressing behavioral, cultural, and motivational factors are needed. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a digital-spiritual assistance Dzikry model in improving maternal hemoglobin status and ANC compliance.MATERIALS AND METHODS:A quasiexperimental nonequivalent control group design with pretest-posttest measurements were conducted among 60 second-trimester pregnant women at a clinic in Tangerang, Indonesia. Participants were allocated to an intervention group receiving digital education, visit reminders, and spiritually oriented motivational support, or a control group receiving standard ANC services. Hemoglobin levels were measured at baseline and follow-up. Secondary outcomes included ANC compliance, maternal knowledge, and perceived communication quality. Data were analyzed using independent t-tests, Chi-square tests, ANCOVA, and logistic regression.RESULTS:Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. The intervention showed a significantly greater increase in Hb levels compared to the control group (mean difference 0.7 g/dL; P = 0.004). A greater reduction in anemia prevalence was also observed. Additionally, the intervention group demonstrated higher ANC compliance, improved knowledge, and better communication scores. Women in the intervention group were more than three times as likely to achieve normal Hb status.CONCLUSIONS:The digital-spiritual assistance Dzikry model effectively enhances maternal engagement in ANC and improves hemoglobin levels, indicating its potential as a culturally adaptive strategy to maternal anemia in primary care settings.

TI Pedagogical determinants of cognitive flexibility among pre-service
   school counselors in Indonesia: A multisite cross-sectional study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Cognitive flexibility; counseling course; pedagogical quality;
   pre-service counselor students
ID PERFORMANCE; REGRESSION; MODEL
AB BACKGROUND:School counselors are mental-health service providers for students, working in complex and unpredictable situations that demand rapid adaptive responding. Cognitive flexibility is the core adaptive skill for this work, but how counselor education can cultivate cognitive flexibility in pre-service school counselors is still not well established. This study aims to investigate the association between the levels of cognitive flexibility and the pedagogical quality of counseling courses that have been implemented in counselor education programs in Indonesia.MATERIALS AND METHODS:A total of 846 pre-service school counselors who had completed theoretical and practical counseling courses under supervision were recruited in this multisite cross-sectional survey study (MAge = 21.44, SD = 2.64). The respondents in our study came from 21 universities in Indonesia. An ordinal logistic regression model was used for statistical analysis.RESULTS:The study found that (a) the scores of theoretical and practical counseling courses under supervisors, (b) students' ratings of their practical counseling course skills, (c) learning materials, (d) learning models, and (e) evaluation learning process significantly contribute to the levels of cognitive flexibility. Odds ratio analysis showedthat respondents who rated their counseling skills as "very good," used "real cases" as learning material, adopted an "active learning model," and used "self-reflection" for learning evaluation were more likely to demonstrate higher levels of their cognitive flexibility (CI = 95%).CONCLUSIONS:This study contributes evidence-based insights for counselor educators and university policy makers to enhance pre-service counselor students' cognitive flexibility through real cases, active learning, and self-reflective evaluation.

TI Health behavior and hygiene practices among islamic boarding school
   students in Indonesia: A qualitative study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Adolescent; health; hygiene; schools; student
AB BACKGROUND:Islamic boarding schools in Indonesia are essential for religious and character education, yet health behavior and hygiene practices (HBHP) among students remain limited, leading to preventable illnesses. This study aimed to explore HBHP in boarding schools, identify supporting and inhibiting factors, and examine the role of community health centers (CHCs) in promoting student health.MATERIALS AND METHODS:A qualitative design with thematic analysis was applied. Nineteen informants were purposively selected, including students, teachers, administrators, caretakers, CHC health promotion officers, and a health department representative. Data were collected through in-depth interviews and participatory observation and then analyzed using Braun and Clarke's framework with NVivo 12 Plus.RESULTS:Five themes emerged: (1) daily hygiene constraints and common health disorders such as skin, digestive, and respiratory problems; (2) psychosocial and academic impacts of illness, including homesickness, reduced concentration, and disrupted religious activities; (3) factors shaping health behavior, including institutional rules, role models, peer influence, and personal habits; (4) the interface between CHCs and boarding schools through counseling, screening, and health programs, constrained by limited resources; and (5) strategies to overcome barriers, such as schedule adjustments, simplified access, and interprogram collaboration.CONCLUSION:The findings highlight that student health in boarding schools is influenced by individual routines, institutional policies, and health system support. Strengthening school rules, teacher role modeling, and consistent CHC involvement are critical to improving HBHP. This study contributes qualitative evidence for culturally grounded health promotion models in Indonesian boarding schools.

TI The effect of self-study training on resilience and effective coping
   style of women involved in domestic violence
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Coping style; domestic violence; education; health promotion; resilience
ID VICTIMS
AB BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE:Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a serious yet preventable public health issue. Resilience plays a significant role in helping women overcome the effects of IPV. The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of self-help training on the resilience of women exposed to IPV.MATERIAL AND METHODS:In this clinical trial, 62 female survivors of violence who were attending comprehensive health service centers in 2022, randomly assigned to either an intervention or a control group. Data collection instruments included a demographic characteristics questionnaire, the Violence Against Women Scale, the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC), and the problem-focused coping subscale of the Ways of Coping Questionnaire (WOCQ) by Lazarus and Folkman. The training in this study was delivered in person using lectures, group discussions, and question-and-answer sessions. The total number of sessions was 14 sessions of 60 min each, for two groups of 16 participants. Data were analyzed using SPSS software (version 21), independent t-tests, and analysis of variance with repeated measures (ANOVA).RESULTS:The results demonstrated a significant increase in resilience scores in the intervention group over time, (baseline 58.27 +/- 19.83, immediately 65.79 +/- 17.77, one month 66.68 +/- 17.49, and two months 66.44 +/- 17.61, post-intervention) (P value: 0.002). And in effective coping style scores (baseline 35.51 +/- 11.64, immediately 43.13 +/- 12.47, one month 43.37 +/- 12.39, and two months 43.86 +/- 12.65, post-intervention) (P value: 0.008).CONCLUSION:Verbal self-instruction improves resilience scores and effective coping styles, but its impact is greater on resilience. This training method can be included in counseling and support programs to optimize healthcare services for women affected by domestic violence.

TI Design and implementation of a pediatric failure to thrive registry
   system in Iran
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Failure to thrive; failure to thrive registry; low weight; registry;
   registry system; stunting
AB BACKGROUND:Failure to thrive (FTT) refers to inadequate growth caused by an inability to acquire or use enough calories for growth. It refers to a failure to develop over time, which can lead to more serious problems in adulthood if left untreated. FTT is a significant global health concern, particularly in developing countries like Iran. Effective FTT management necessitates timely, inclusive, and precise data on children's FTT status. A pediatric FTT registry system is a useful tool for gathering and managing data on children with FTT. This study proposes a pediatric FTT registry system for Iran.MATERIALS AND METHODS:A developmental-applied study was conducted in three phases during 2024. The first phase involved defining the features of a pediatric FTT registry system through interviews with experts. The second phase entailed expert validation using the Delphi method. In the third phase, the software was designed based on a conceptual model using the Hypertext Preprocessor programming language and the Laravel framework. PostgreSQL was employed as the database management system. Moreover, Nielsen's Ten Usability Heuristics was used to evaluate the software's usability from the users' perspectives.RESULTS:Experts validated the features of the pediatric FTT registry system, resulting in a framework that included eight headings, 24 sub-headings, and 117 data elements. The usability assessment of the software revealed that the highest number of issues concerned the "error prevention" indicator, whereas the "aesthetic and minimalist design" indicator presented the fewest problems and was assumed flawless.CONCLUSION:A pediatric FFT registry system contributes significantly to service planning, management, disease surveillance, and research. Accordingly, future research is recommended to investigate the feasibility of implementing the pediatric FFT registry system in Iran.

TI Enhancing public awareness: Insights from mothers and healthcare experts
   on postpartum depression - A qualitative study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Health education; maternal health; mental health literacy; postpartum
   depression; video intervention
ID STIGMA
AB BACKGROUND:Pregnancy and early motherhood represent periods of significant psychological vulnerability. An estimated 10-15% of mothers experience postpartum depression (PPD) annually in India. Maternal mental health (MMH) represents a critical public health concern, impacting both maternal and child well-being. This study constitutes the first qualitative exploration in India to examine perspectives of both mothers and healthcare professionals regarding PPD for the development of culturally appropriate educational intervention.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This qualitative exploratory study, conducted from April to August 2023, employed three focus group discussions among a total of 25 participants: 14 mothers attending immunization clinics at urban and rural primary health centres, and 11 healthcare professionals with expertise in MMH. Semi-structured discussion guides facilitated exploration of PPD awareness, cultural beliefs, barriers, and intervention preferences. Audio recordings were transcribed verbatim and analyzed using thematic analysis.RESULTS:Five distinct themes emerged across two participant categories: PPD awareness, barriers to help-seeking, impact of PPD, management strategies, and video intervention preferences. Findings revealed a lack of PPD awareness among mothers. Public health experts perceived an increasing trend in the occurrence of PPD in rural settings. Both groups endorsed video interventions as effective tools, emphasizing it to be concise, available in regional language, and a multi-platform dissemination strategy.CONCLUSION:This qualitative study reveals substantial knowledge gaps regarding PPD and suggests video interventions as effective tools towards awareness promotion. Culturally relevant educational interventions hold strong potential to enhance PPD literacy. Integrating these insights would enable health policy frameworks to strengthen early identification systems and improve care pathways.

TI Examination of students' perspectives regarding the effectiveness of
   clinical training: A research endeavor congruent with social
   responsibility
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Education; preceptorship; social responsibility; students
AB BACKGROUND:Clinical education is a fundamental component of medical training. This study examines the experiences of clinical students across various health professions to provide valuable insights for educational planners involved in designing effective and socially relevant clinical training curricula.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This descriptive-analytical study employed a stratified random sampling method to select clinical students from the disciplines of nursing, midwifery, operating room technology, and pre-hospital emergency medicine at educational institutions in Shoushtar. Data were gathered using a standardized questionnaire designed to evaluate factors affecting the quality of clinical education. The data were analyzed using Pearson correlation, Chi-square tests, independent t-tests, and analysis of variance (ANOVA).RESULTS:A total of 190 students participated in the study, including 60 males and 130 females, with ages ranging from 18 to 39 years. Participants were enrolled in nursing (n = 105), operating room technology (n = 30), midwifery (n = 40), and emergency medicine (n = 15) programs. Male students reported significantly lower scores in areas related to student-teacher interactions, the learning environment, and evaluation criteria. Notably, overall clinical education scores demonstrated a decreasing trend with increasing age. Emergency medicine students achieved the highest scores, while those in nursing and operating room programs recorded the lowest.CONCLUSIONS:The mean scores related to educational objectives, instructor quality, student-teacher interactions, and the learning environment were lower among male students, older participants, and those enrolled in nursing and operating room programs. These findings highlight the need for targeted educational interventions to improve clinical training objectives, enhance the involvement of qualified instructors, and foster more supportive learning environments.

TI The relationship between health literacy and the adoption of preventive
   behaviors against high blood pressure among villagers: A cross-sectional
   study in Iran
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Health literacy; high blood pressure; preventive behaviors; villagers
ID HYPERTENSION; POPULATION
AB BACKGROUND:Considering the limited number of studies on health literacy among the rural population, the necessity of measuring the level of health literacy, and the increasing number of patients with hypertension, the present study aimed to determine the relationship between health literacy and the adoption of preventive behaviors in high blood pressure among the villagers.MATERIALS AND METHODS:In a descriptive-analytical cross-sectional study, 300 villagers living in Qayenat were selected by multi-stage random sampling in 2024. The data were obtained by demographic and background characteristics and the health literacy assessment questionnaire (HELIA) as well as a valid and reliable questionnaire to measure the adoption of preventive behaviors against hypertension. The data were analyzed using SPSS ver 22. (IBM Coporation, Armonk, NY) and descriptive statistics and logistic regression.RESULTS:The mean and standard deviation of adoption of preventive behaviors against hypertension and health literacy were 15.188 +/- 1.215 and 61.07 +/- 18.206, respectively, and both were at an unfavorable level. Health literacy, the number of children, the amount of physical activity per week, and the history of having high blood pressure were effective factors in adopting preventive behaviors against high blood pressure.CONCLUSION:The adoption of preventive behaviors against hypertension was lower among villagers with lower health literacy, having more children, less physical activity per week, and those who had no history of hypertension. Therefore, community health policymakers must design educational interventions in health literacy and hypertension prevention to help improve these patients' health.

TI Developing a model for conflict management in intensive care units: A
   grounded theory study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Conflicts; conflict management; grounded theory; intensive care units;
   nurses; qualitative research
AB BACKGROUND:Conflict is a very common phenomenon in the intensive care unit (ICU). Nonetheless, the aim of conflict-related strategies is not to eliminate conflicts but to effectively manage them. The aim of this study was to develop a model for conflict management (CM) in the ICU.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This qualitative study was conducted in 2024 by using Corbin and Strauss's grounded theory design. Data were collected via 32 semi-structured interviews with 18 ICU nurses, observational notes, field notes, and memo writing. Participants were purposefully selected from hospitals affiliated to Zanjan University of Medical Sciences, Zanjan, Iran. Corbin and Strauss's method was used to analyze the data. Then, Walker and Avant's method was used to develop a prescriptive CM model.RESULTS:Participants' main concern was a vicious relational cycle, and their strategy for its management was striving to build CM-based relational bridges. The outcome of this strategy was doubtfulness over compromise or silence. The compromise-based relationship model for CM was developed with three main components, namely the management of the situation, awareness of CM strategies, and development of communication skills.CONCLUSION:The CM process depends on the sociocultural characteristics of nurses and healthcare organizations. The establishment of appropriate relationships is the key prerequisite to CM and depends on the development of nurses' professional skills and strong organizational support. Therefore, health policymakers should consider developing communication and CM skills in nurses.

TI Telenutrition health education program to increase nutritional
   awareness, attitude, and dietary diversity among secondary high school
   adolescent girls in rural area of Bangladesh: A quasi-experimental study
   protocol
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Adolescent girls; Bangladesh; dietary diversity; malnutrition; rural
   area; telenutrition
ID MATERNAL UNDERWEIGHT; NUTRIENT ADEQUACY; UNDERNUTRITION; BURDEN
AB BACKGROUND:Telenutrition, using telehealth technologies for remote nutritional care, has proven effective in primary care. Nutritional deficiencies constitute a global health burden, characterized by chronic undernutrition and micronutrient deficiencies, especially in adolescent girls in impoverished nations such as Bangladesh. Telenutrition, which uses digital technologies to provide remote nutritional treatment, is a promising strategy to decrease this burden. This study aims to determine the impact of telenutrition education on improving nutritional awareness, attitude, and dietary diversity among school going adolescent girls in rural Bangladesh.MATERIALS AND METHODS:A school-based quasi-experimental study was conducted among 190 adolescent girls (95 intervention, 95 control) from two higher secondary schools in Sakhipur, Bangladesh. Schools were allocated into intervention and control groups using a coin toss method to reduce selection bias and to mitigate the risk of contamination of health education information among students within the same school. Interviewers used structured questionnaires to gather baseline data on socio-demographic traits, nutrition-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices, dietary diversity, food hygiene, sanitation, and menstrual hygiene. The intervention group received six months of nutrition-focused education, covered video sessions, text messages, and follow-up phone calls, while the control group received no intervention. The primary outcome of this study is changes in nutritional awareness, attitudes, and practice scores among adolescents. Additionally, secondary outcomes include improvements in dietary diversity and changes in BMI, hip-waist circumference, and MUAC that will be compared across groups over time. The effects of the intervention will be evaluated over time using mixed-effects models in STATA 18.5.RESULTS:Data analysis will commence after implementation collection, with findings prepared for publication.CONCLUSION:Telenutrition education is expected to effectively enhance knowledge and promote healthy behaviors among adolescent girls. Digital health programs, policy-driven approaches, and school-based nutrition education are essential for improving nutritional awareness.

TI Impact of music therapy on diabetes distress and bio-physiological
   parameters in patients with diabetic foot ulcer
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Diabetes mellitus; diabetic foot; music therapy; patients
ID PREVALENCE; MANAGEMENT
AB BACKGROUND:Diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) is a common and significant complication of uncontrolled diabetes mellitus (DM), frequently resulting in increased physiological suffering and emotional burden. Music therapy, as a complementary intervention, has shown potential in lowering stress and improving general well-being, but its influence on patients with DFU is unknown. The present study aimed to identify the impact of music therapy on diabetes distress and bio-physiological parameters among patients with DFU.METHODS AND MATERIALS:The study was conducted in a selected tertiary care hospital in South India, and a Quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group research design was used. A non-probability purposive sampling was used to select 159 participants with DFU into three groups: Group I (n = 53) received patient-selected music therapy, Group II (n = 53) received researcher-selected music, and the control group (n = 53) received routine treatment only. The intervention involved listening to music for 20 minutes twice daily over 21 consecutive days, along with standard medical care. Ethical clearance was obtained from the institutional review board and ethics committee. Data were analyzed by descriptive and inferential statistics using SPSS version 26.RESULTS:The study shows a statistically significant (p < 0.001) difference within Groups I, II, compared to the control group for diabetes distress and all the bio-physiological parameters. However, the mean posttest scores of diabetes distress and bio-physiological parameters in Groups I and II were considerably reduced from the mean pretest scores compared to the control group.CONCLUSION:The study finding helps to integrate music therapy as a complementary therapy for people with DFU to preserve good physical and mental health.

TI Academic Literacy Issue in Thesis Writing Among Education Students
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE Academic Literacy; Plagiarism Practices; Prevalence; Thesis Writing;
   Teacher Education
AB This study examined the manifestation of plagiarism among education students, as a basis for a literacy program. Employing a descriptive-correlational research design, 18 undergraduate thesis papers were analysed using Turnitin, followed by multiple regression to identify factors influencing similarity rates. Results revealed that 78 percent of the papers exceeded the acceptable 20 percent similarity threshold, with copy-paste practices from bound theses and online sources without proper citation as the most common violation. The study concludes that addressing pedagogical deficiencies through enhanced research mentoring and explicit writing instruction is essential for fostering ethical scholarly practices in higher education.

TI School Music Teachers on Television: Identity and Practice
SO EDUCATION SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE music education; music teachers; musician identity; music teacher
   identity; music teacher preparation; musicianship; teacher
   characteristics; music teaching techniques; television
AB This study examines how school music teachers are represented in English-language television series and considers implications for professional identity, pedagogy and recruitment. Drawing on a novel, systematically coded database of 36 on-screen music educators from 28 television series from 1952 to 2026, quantitative description maps demographic attributes (age, gender, ethnicity, socioeconomic status), narrative role (minor, major, protagonist), genre and institutional context. Our findings show music teachers are most often supporting characters, typically mid-career, male and predominantly white, with comedy-especially ensemble school comedy-dominating portrayals. Qualitative interpretation demonstrates persistent teacher archetypes and pedagogical tropes: the failed performer turned teacher, the inspirational mentor who singles out a talented student, and blurred teacher-student boundaries. This article situates these findings within contemporary concerns about teacher shortages and declining occupational status in English-language contexts, arguing that mediated images may influence career choice, teacher retention and societal attitudes. Methodological advances include expanded time and geographic contexts of studied texts and detailed coding. The paper concludes by calling for reception and experimental studies to test causal effects on aspiring teachers and to inform teacher education curricula.

TI The Uneven Convertibility of Family Cultural Capital to Academic
   Engagement and Research Self-Efficacy Among Chinese Graduate Students
   with Rural and Urban Backgrounds
SO EDUCATION SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE family cultural capital; academic engagement; research self-efficacy;
   rural-urban background; graduate education
AB This study examined how different forms of family cultural capital are linked to Chinese graduate students' academic engagement and research self-efficacy, and whether these pathways differ by rural-urban background. Drawing on cultural capital theory and social cognitive theory, the study distinguished embodied, objectified, and institutionalized family cultural capital and conceptualized academic engagement as a behavioral pathway through which family-based resources may become relevant to research. Survey data were collected from 412 graduate students at five public universities in China. Partial least squares structural equation modeling with 5000 bootstrap resamples was used to test direct and indirect pathways separately for students from rural and urban backgrounds. The results showed that embodied family cultural capital was positively related to academic engagement in both groups, and academic engagement was positively related to research self-efficacy. Academic engagement mediated the relationship between embodied family cultural capital and research self-efficacy for both rural- and urban-background students. However, embodied family cultural capital only had a significant direct relationship with research self-efficacy among urban-background students. Objectified family cultural capital was only negatively related to research self-efficacy among rural-background students, while institutionalized family cultural capital showed no significant relationships in either group. These findings suggest that family cultural capital is not uniformly converted into research self-efficacy in graduate education. Its role depends on the form of cultural capital and the rural-urban context in which academic engagement is enacted. Theoretically, this study shows that the conversion of family cultural capital into research self-efficacy is form-specific and context-dependent. Practically, it identifies academic engagement as a key leverage point for promoting equitable research development among graduate students from diverse family backgrounds.

TI Path optimization and temporal overtaking: a mechanical analogy teaching
   model
SO EUROPEAN JOURNAL OF PHYSICS
LA English
DT Article
DE path optimization; brachistochrone; overtaking phenomenon; mechanical
   analogy; physics teaching
AB Systems that start farther from their target can, counterintuitively, arrive sooner. Such nonmonotonic relaxation phenomena appear across physics, chemistry, and biology. This paper takes the brachistochrone problem as a mechanical entry point and constructs a teaching analogy model in which the path of descent is freely configurable: two point masses start from different heights and slide without friction to a common endpoint along independently chosen paths. Taking the red ball on a cycloid (the brachistochrone) and the blue ball on an inclined straight line as the canonical case, a rigorous mathematical analysis proves the existence of a parameter interval-which we call the overtaking zone-in which the higher-starting red ball reaches the endpoint before the blue ball, demonstrating the logical structure 'path optimization leads to temporal reversal' within classical mechanics. The model does not construct a microscopic mechanism for real thermal relaxation; its pedagogical contribution is to provide a precise, transparent, and interactive mechanical demonstration platform for the concept of path dependence, a fundamental idea in nonequilibrium statistical physics. An interactive simulation tool accompanies the paper, along with a teaching discussion framework.

TI Sagnac effect, an easy way to a relativistic experiment
SO EUROPEAN JOURNAL OF PHYSICS
LA English
DT Article
DE Sagnac effect; optical fiber interferometer; birefringence; rotating
   frame of reference in special relativity; theory choice based on numbers
AB An inexpensive interferometer, in which infrared light travels through ordinary telecommunications optical fiber, is described. In one section of the fiber, two waves travel in opposite directions, so that when the device is rotated, it exhibits the Sagnac effect. A digital display allows direct visual observation, and the effect is even visible when the device is slowly rotated in the hands. The theoretical model is developed and requires only basic knowledge of optics (polarized light, birefringent medium) and special relativity (laws of length contraction and time dilation, laws of velocity composition). The article introduces useful higher-level concepts (rotating frame of reference, comoving frames of reference). The calculations are then carried out in a very concrete experimental context. Quantitative observations are clearly in good agreement with relativistic kinematics and not at all with Galilean kinematics. The interferometer at rest also allows the observation of unusual optical effects.

TI Predicting Student Dropout from Pre-Enrollment Data in Mexican Higher
   Education: A Theoretically Grounded and Calibrated Machine Learning
   Approach
SO EDUCATION SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE student dropout; dropout prediction; early warning system; machine
   learning; ensemble methods; pre-enrollment data; theoretical grounding;
   educational data mining
ID MODEL; RETENTION
AB Featured Application The proposed model can be integrated into an institutional dashboard to report dropout risk by student, cohort, academic program, and campus, and to facilitate the prioritization of mentoring, academic support, and early intervention strategies.Abstract Student dropout remains a persistent challenge in higher education, with significant academic, social and institutional implications. Although machine learning (ML) models for dropout prediction have proliferated, most select input variables based on data availability rather than theory and rarely report psychometric validation of the constructs used. This study addresses both gaps by developing and validating an early warning system at a Mexican university using exclusively pre-enrollment data from more than 46,000 student records from 2014 to 2025. Following the CRISP-DM methodology, eight theoretically grounded constructs, anchored in Tinto's integration model, Bean's attrition model, and Cabrera et al.'s persistence model, were operationalized from institutional intake questionnaires and assessed for internal consistency using Cronbach's alpha prior to model training. Eight supervised ML algorithms were benchmarked across distance-based (Logistic Regression, SVM, AdaBoost, ANN) and tree-based (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) families. A tuned and isotonically calibrated Random Forest achieved the best overall performance (recall = 0.743, F1 = 0.524, ROC-AUC = 0.734, PR-AUC = 0.478) on a strictly held-out test set that was not used at any stage of model development. The 2023-2025 cohorts, whose dropout labels were not yet observable under the institutional definition, were scored prospectively to generate operational risk profiles. SHAP analysis identified high-school GPA, parental education, and household asset indices as dominant predictors, which mapped directly onto the three theoretical frameworks. These findings demonstrate that psychometrically grounded pre-enrollment data alone can support an operationally deployable dropout detection system, enabling proactive, evidence-based retention interventions from the first day of enrollment.

   Geography Teachers: A Mixed-Methods Study

   JOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Curriculum literacy; curriculum autonomy; fidelity to the curriculum;
   curriculum; geography teacher
ID IMPLEMENTATION; PREVENTION; EDUCATION
AB In this study, the effects of geography teachers' curriculum literacy and curriculum autonomy levels on their levels of fidelity to the curriculum have been investigated. The study was conducted using an explanatory sequential design, a mixed-methods research approach. A total of 416 geography teachers selected via simple random sampling for the quantitative component and 10 geography teachers selected via purposive sampling for the qualitative component participated in the study. Quantitative data were collected using scales measuring curriculum literacy, curriculum autonomy, and fidelity to the curriculum; qualitative data were collected through semi-structured interviews. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistical techniques, correlation and multiple linear regression analysis, and content analysis. Quantitative findings indicated that teachers' levels of curriculum literacy, curriculum autonomy, and fidelity to the curriculum were generally high. Qualitative findings also revealed that these perceptions, which appeared high at the quantitative level, were reflected in classroom practices only partially and in a context-sensitive manner. The discrepancy between quantitative and qualitative findings can be attributed to the fact that while quantitative data reflect self-reported perceptions, qualitative data make contextual constraints - such as time constraints and exam pressure - that teachers encounter in practice more apparent. As a result, it was determined that teachers' fidelity to and autonomy regarding the curriculum manifest as adapted fidelity and partial autonomy rather than full alignment.

AB This study examines global publication trends and the intellectual structure of research on Universities of the Third Age (U3A) and later-life learning through bibliometric analysis. To achieve this, a case study was conducted. Activities related to the graded teaching model in textbooks were examined; the application of the model by 10 Turkish language teachers was observed by the researcher; and the teachers' opinions about the model were collected. The data were analyzed through content analysis. Teaching writing skills and cognitive strategies is targeted in Turkish language textbooks within the scope of the gradual release of responsibility model. Teachers indicated that the similarity and abundance of activities in the textbooks made implementation timeconsuming and negatively affected student motivation. It was also observed that teachers faced challenges in implementing the model due to factors such as large class sizes, physical conditions, and students' readiness.

TI Evaluating Human Reviewers versus Artificial Intelligence: A Comparative
   Analysis of AI-Generated Essay Detection in Higher Education
SO PAMUKKALE UNIVERSITESI EGITIM FAKULTESI DERGISI-PAMUKKALE UNIVERSITY
   JOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE AI-generated text detection; academic integrity; English language
   teaching; automated essay evaluation
AB The proliferation of AI text generation tools in educational settings has created unprecedented challenges for academic integrity. As AI-generated content grows more sophisticated, traditional assessment methods may no longer suffice to distinguish human from machine-authored work. This mixed-methods study compared human reviewers, an AI scoring model, and plagiarism detection tools in identifying AI-generated essays. Sixteen essays were analyzed: eight by ELT master's students and eight AI-generated (ChatGPT 4o, Gemini 1.5, Llama), with four subsequently humanized. ELT was selected because writing proficiency and authentic voice are central disciplinary competencies. Two faculty reviewers, iThenticate, Turnitin, and a GPT-4o model evaluated all essays using an expert-reviewed analytic rubric covering coherence, originality, depth, writing style, and topic adherence. The AI model showed superior internal consistency (alpha = 0.923) versus human reviewers (alpha = 0.832). Turnitin achieved the highest accuracy (87.5%). Human reviewers performed inconsistently (62.5%; Fisher's Exact Test, p = .096). Inter-rater agreement was assessed via quadratic weighted kappa (QWK), as small sample sizes precluded a valid chi-square analysis. Digital tools currently outperform human judgment in detecting AI-generated content, yet limitations persist across all methods. These findings underscore the need for institutional AI policies, educator training, and hybrid human-technological assessment approaches.

   Quality of School Life

AB This study examined the structural relationships among students' school motivation, perceived ethical behaviors of teachers, and the quality of school life related to school management. TI Trust in Science
SO AMERICAN BIOLOGY TEACHER
LA English
DT Article
DE trust in science; ancestry testing; vaccines; mistrust; distrust; nature
   of science; socioscientific issues
ID VACCINES; AUTISM
AB Trust in science should mean neither uncritical deference nor sweeping skepticism, but a calibrated, reflective stance. To illustrate what this stance requires, I examine two contrasting, context-specific cases. Commercial DNA ancestry tests illustrate gullibility, as probabilistic estimates are often marketed and interpreted as precise revelations of identity, even though genetic ancestry captures only a limited subset of genealogical ancestry. By contrast, vaccine-autism debates illustrate mistrust: despite extensive evidence against a causal link, political identity, conspiracist ideation, and misleading public discourse sustain doubt and confuse absence of evidence for a link with lack of grounds to reject it. I argue that appropriate trust in science lies in the reliability of scientific methods, communities, and institutions over time. Science education should therefore help students understand how scientific knowledge is produced, evaluated, and used.

TI Disrupting Homeostasis in the Classroom
SO AMERICAN BIOLOGY TEACHER
LA English
DT Article
DE sexism; higher education; biological sciences; gender inequity;
   inclusivity
ID GENDER BIAS; CAREER; STEM
AB Despite women achieving gender parity in undergraduate biological sciences programs, systemic sexism persists, eroding their confidence, sense of belonging, and career aspirations. This phenomenon can be likened to "cultural apoptosis," where the exclusionary dynamics within academic environments function like a biological process, eliminating diversity and stifling innovation. Dismissive behaviors, microaggressions, and inequitable access to mentorship and resources contribute to this cultural apoptosis, reinforcing systemic barriers that hinder women's academic engagement and professional development. This article highlights the need to move beyond numerical representation and address the cultural and institutional factors that perpetuate these inequities. Drawing on research findings, it provides actionable recommendations for postsecondary biology faculty to create inclusive classrooms that empower all students. These strategies include, but are not limited to, fostering inclusive mentorship programs, implementing collaborative learning approaches, addressing implicit biases through faculty training, and establishing transparent resource allocation policies. By challenging cultural apoptosis and promoting equity-focused practices, faculty can play a transformative role in supporting women in biology and cultivating a more diverse and innovative STEM workforce.

TI The Effect of Grading Policies Used for Second-Chance Testing on Student
   Achievement in an Introductory Biology Course
SO AMERICAN BIOLOGY TEACHER
LA English
DT Article
DE retakes; mastery-based testing; alternative grading
ID PERFORMANCE; COLLEGE
AB In order to address underperformance and low retention in a majors introductory biology course, we implemented second-chance testing, hypothesizing that it would lead to an increase in exam grades. We divided the course content into 16 learning outcomes (LOs). Students tested over 3-4 LOs at a time during in-class exam days and had the option to retest on a limited number of LOs during in-class retake days. We implemented two different grading policies over two fall semesters. In one iteration we used a full replacement + insurance policy (i.e., Policy 1) in which only the highest grade for each LO exam was counted. In the second iteration, the exam score was calculated by weighting the lowest attempt at 25% and the highest attempt at 75% (i.e., Policy 2). Analysis of first-attempt and retake exam grades showed that students increased their LO exam average by similar to 14% through the use of second-chance testing under both grading policies. Students retested more often under Policy 1 and students earning >= 90% on a first-attempt LO exam retested only under Policy 1. Students earning < 70% on a first-attempt LO exam were more likely to retest under both policies compared with students earning a passing grade. A majority of students earning < 60% on a first-attempt exam were unable to achieve a passing grade for that LO through retesting, regardless of policy. Our data support the conclusion that second-chance testing can be used by students to make significant grade improvements and is especially important for students earning a D on a first-attempt exam. When using a modular approach in which many smaller exams are used, we recommend a full replacement + insurance grading policy due to higher rates of participation.
